00b65358356d3cf6835d.description: Product Manager - Products and Pricing Location: London, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office) Salary: £50,000 – £60,000 Team: Energy Commerce Contract: Permanent Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities . About Kaluza Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future. Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life. With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen. What you’ll do Lead the localisation efforts for our products and pricing capabilities, ensuring they meet the specific commercial, regulatory, market, and cultural requirements of retailers in Europe.  This will include European localisations such as indexation and unbundled energy products as well as broader market promotions and discounts. Deep dive into European energy market structures and regulations for designated countries, translating complex needs into detailed product specifications.  Understand the broader context of piercing and selling products in Europe and the required tooling, workflows and models to accelerate our retailers Collaborate intensely with clients and in-country experts to understand their unique needs and requirements. You will be the first point of contact with the client for all domain specific needs. Coordinate cross domain discovery and delivery for features that support key journeys, aligning requirements where needed (eg. billing, quoting and energy insights). Define and manage detailed product requirements for features related to country-specific needs to support energy products and pricing. Contribute to the Global Energy Commerce roadmap , when new acceleration opportunities are identified. Work closely with engineering, UX, and QA teams to ensure the successful implementation and testing of localised billing functionalities. Act as the go-to expert for global teams on specific European market nuances related to energy products and pricing and related customer journeys. (Note: Travel to client sites e.g., Brussels, is expected at roughly 1–3 trips a month initially, tapering to 1–2 times a quarter.) What you’ll bring Ideally, you’ll have: Proven experience as a Product Manager with a strong track record of successfully localising complex software products for international markets. Able to establish and maintain great relationships with B2B clients , throughout the entire product lifecycle. Solid understanding of the end-to-end energy lifecycle within a European context, with a particular focus on retailer commercial operations. Direct experience with specific European energy markets, understanding their unique regulatory frameworks and requirements Exceptional ability to translate abstract regulatory text or client requirements into clear, actionable requirements for development teams. Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (engineering, legal, operations, client success) to deliver localised solutions. Experience working alongside multiple services/domains to deliver complex journeys. Excellent communication skills , able to articulate technical and market complexities to various stakeholders, including clients. What will set you apart Deep, hands-on experience with the French or Belgian energy retail markets , particularly concerning their energy products and pricing specificities. Proficiency in a second European language relevant to key target markets (e.g., French). Experience with large-scale data migration and integration projects involving legacy billing systems. A background in energy commercial operations or regulatory affairs within a European energy retailer. Where you'll work We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week. Our Values Five values guide how we work at Kaluza: Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale. Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes. Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say. Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego. Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives. Our Perks Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget Climate: Furthr, our climate action app We want the best people We’re keen to meet people from all walks of life — our view is that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We want to build teams which represent a variety of experiences, perspectives and skills, and we recognise talent on the basis of merit and potential. Come as you are We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you. Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn . Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here . 00f8be4e178a6dfff46d.description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person. We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform. This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch. We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one. This role will be based in London , UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin. What you'll do: Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers. Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout. Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times. Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer. Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter. Job Description: 2027 Technology Internship - AI-Native Data Platform Engineering - 6-month Internship (January – July) TD Securities are offering an exceptional opportunity to join a diverse and dynamic team through our 6-month Technology Internship on the AI- Native  Data Platform Engineering team. Internship Overview Contract Type: Full-time, 6-Month Internship Dates: January 2027 – July 2027 Location: Dublin Office : 1 Molesworth Street Candidates must have an unrestricted right to work in Ireland throughout the entire duration of the internship. Team Overview: The TDS Data Platform Engineering team is building the next generation of data platforms where data products, AI agents, and self-service analytics work together to help users discover, understand, and consume data more effectively. Our mission is to provide a scalable, secure, and AI-ready data platform that empowers domain teams to build and own data products while enabling consumers to interact with data through modern experiences such as AI agents, natural language interfaces, and intelligent automation. As a Graduate Analyst or a 6-month Intern, you will help shape how AI and data platforms converge. You will work on technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs), Agentic AI, Model Context Protocol (MCP), data products, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and analytics solutions. You will collaborate with domain owners, data engineers, application teams, and platform engineers to create innovative solutions that make data easier to discover, understand, and use. We are a highly collaborative team that values curiosity, experimentation, continuous learning, and delivering business value through simple, scalable, and user-centric solutions. How you will Contribute: Help design and build AI-ready data platform capabilities that enable self-service data discovery and usage. Develop AI agents and MCP-based integrations that allow users to interact with data products using natural language. Collaborate with domain owners to understand their data products and create intelligent experiences that simplify data consumption. Build APIs, services, and automation frameworks that expose data and business capabilities to AI agents and applications. Contribute to the development of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions using enterprise data sources. Assist in building and maintaining scalable data pipelines and cloud-native data services. Create proof-of-concepts exploring emerging technologies in AI, data engineering, and developer productivity. Partner with platform users to understand pain points and improve platform usability and adoption. Develop tools that help users discover datasets, understand lineage, definitions, ownership, and usage patterns. Support the implementation of governance, security, and access controls for AI-enabled solutions. Participate in platform monitoring, troubleshooting, testing, and continuous improvement activities. Contribute to technical documentation, architecture reviews, and knowledge-sharing initiatives. Apply engineering best practices including clean code, automated testing, CI/CD, and secure software development. Continuously research emerging AI and data technologies and evaluate their relevance to the platform. Key Technologies: The successful graduate will gain experience in: AI Agents, Agentic Workflows, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and Prompt Engineering Java (Spring Boot) for APIs and backend services Python for data engineering, automation, analytics, and AI solutions Apache Spark and Dremio for large-scale data processing and data products Azure Data Platform Ecosystem including Databricks, AKS, ADLS, ADF, and Azure AI Services Vector Databases and Semantic Search technologies REST APIs, gRPC, and Event-Driven Architectures Kafka for real-time data movement GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, and Confluence Observability platforms such as Dynatrace and Datadog Security, Governance, and Data Catalog technologies Who we are looking for: Penultimate year student in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. Bachelors or Masters programme. Passion for solving business problems using data and AI. Strong curiosity and willingness to explore emerging technologies. Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with a bias toward learning and experimentation. Interest in understanding both technology and business domains. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills. Programming experience in one or more languages such as Java, Python, JavaScript, or C#. Understanding of APIs and modern software development principles. Basic SQL and data modelling knowledge. Familiarity with Git and collaborative software development practices. Interest in AI, machine learning, large language models, or intelligent systems. Previous experience with the below considered an asset: Experience with Generative AI, LLMs, RAG, AI Agents, or MCP. Knowledge of data engineering concepts and distributed data processing. Exposure to cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, or GCP.o   Familiarity with Databricks, Spark, Dremio, or similar analytics platforms. Understanding of vector databases and semantic search concepts. Experience building APIs using Spring Boot, FastAPI, or similar frameworks. Knowledge of containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. Passion for creating intuitive user experiences and self-service platforms. Interest in Data Mesh, data products, data governance, and AI-enabled analytics. Please note, in order to be considered for the position you must be available for 6-month internship placement, January – July 2027 How to Apply: All applicants are required to submit their CV and a Cover Letter. Only complete applications will be accepted. TD offers a full range of financial products and services more than 25 million customers worldwide through three key business lines: Canadian Retail including TD Canada Trust, Business Banking, TD Auto Finance (Canada), TD Wealth (Canada), TD Direct Investing and TD Insurance U.S. Retail including TD Bank, America’s Most Convenient Bank, TD Auto Finance (U.S.), TD Wealth (U.S.) and TD’s investment in TD Ameritrade Wholesale Banking including TD Securities TD Securities is a leading global corporate and investment bank, delivering capital markets products, advisory services, trading expertise and market insights to corporate, government and institutional clients worldwide. Operating in 30 cities across the globe, we combine deep industry knowledge, innovation and global connectivity to help clients achieve their ambitions. Through our offices in London, Dublin and Belfast, we support clients across the UK, Ireland and Europe while leveraging the strength of our global platform and expertise. We are growth-oriented, people-focused, and community-minded. As a team, we work to deliver value for our clients every day. Inclusiveness At TD, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodation), please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs. Who We Are TD Securities is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. 01b881af17a60a30972b.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

AI is changing what security teams can do. Claude can find and help fix vulnerabilities in code at a pace that wasn't possible a year ago, and we want defenders to have that advantage first. 

As Manager, Cybersecurity Sales Specialists, you'll build and lead the team of cybersecurity specialists who sell to security teams across our Americas business units, including financial services, healthcare and life sciences, and technology. Your team partners with the Account Executives in each industry to lead the security strategy and the security deal with CISOs.

You'll help shape how Anthropic sells security: how your team covers the business units, how it works with the Account Executive and Applied AI organizations, and how what we learn from customers shapes what we build. The work matters to our mission: a safe transition through transformative AI depends on the people who defend critical systems being able to use it well, and this team is how we get it into their hands.


Responsibilities

  • Hire, onboard and develop a high-performing team of cybersecurity sales specialists

  • Own your team's forecast, pipeline health and results across the business units you cover

  • Set your team's coverage model, and agree on clear rules of engagement with the sales leaders who own each industry and with Applied AI leadership on discovery, proofs of concept and architecture

  • Build a pipeline engine with the Account Executives, across their existing accounts and through outbound to security leaders, events and partners

  • Coach your team through complex deals that lead with the customer's problem (finding and fixing vulnerabilities, application security, security operations, and deploying AI agents securely), and act as executive sponsor with CISOs on the most important ones

  • Make security reviews, verification for security use cases, and procurement a repeatable path rather than a deal-by-deal effort

  • Scale enablement so Account Executives across every business unit can spot and qualify security opportunities

  • Bring what your team hears from security customers to sales leadership and to our product, safeguards and marketing teams, and turn it into input on the roadmap

  • Run a healthy team: clear expectations, regular feedback, and performance and development conversations

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience building and leading a cybersecurity sales team that carried a number, whether direct, specialist or overlay, including hiring, coaching and managing performance

  • Track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals where the security organization was the buyer or the deciding approver, and of coaching others to do the same

  • Fluency in how security teams work, built by selling directly to CISOs, application security leads and security engineers

  • Depth in at least one security domain, such as application security, vulnerability management, security operations, cloud, data, identity or endpoint security

  • History of building a business before there was an established approach, through outbound and partners rather than inherited accounts

  • Ability to lead through influence as well as authority, so that Account Executives and their leaders bring your team in because it helps them win

  • Consultative approach to selling and coaching: understanding the problem before proposing anything, and being honest about what a product can't do

  • Commitment to making AI systems safe and beneficial

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background selling security in one of the industries we cover, and an understanding of how security is bought and regulated there

  • Experience managing managers and individual contributors, or scaling a sales team through fast growth

  • Experience leading teams selling AI, developer or data platform products to technical buyers

  • Time spent as a security practitioner or sales engineer before moving into sales leadership

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$450,000—$550,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

028bc3e2dc0d7ea323c7.description: Description Database Migration for Amazon RDS is fully managed, serverless capability that enables customers to migrate SQL Server/Oracle workloads - whether running on Amazon RDS, Amazon EC2, on-premises infrastructure, or other cloud providers - to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Customers simply provide source and target connection details, and the service orchestrates the entire migration lifecycle end-to-end: pre-migration assessment, schema conversion, data movement. In addition to a traditional console-driven experience, the service introduces an agentic migration workflow. Customers can initiate and manage migrations through natural language within the developer tools they already use - such as Kiro, Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. The AI agent assesses the source environment, converts the schema, moves the data, validates the outcome - removing friction and reducing the expertise required to complete complex database migrations. Amazon RDS is a part of AWS Utility Computing (UC) which provides product innovations - from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (Iot), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS, including support for customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services Key job responsibilities Design and implement scalable, serverless microservices that power the migration lifecycle - assessment, schema conversion, data movement; Develop intelligent, agent-driven migration workflows that integrate with modern developer tools and leverage natural language interfaces; Own the end-to-end migration lifecycle - from pre-migration assessment and schema conversion through data movement phases; Solve hard distributed systems challenges around reliability, security, and performance for customers migrating their most critical production workloads; Work at the intersection of cloud infrastructure and AI/ML to deliver a seamless, low-friction migration experience that removes traditional barriers to database modernization; Mentor SDE Is through code reviews, design guidance, and pair programming; Participate in on-call rotations and operational excellence initiatives. A day in the life You might start the day with participating in a design review for a new feature: parallel data movement for multi-terabyte databases. You whiteboard trade-offs between consistency guarantees and throughput, debating how to minimize downtime during cutover windows. Later, you pair with a teammate to debug a race condition in the serverless orchestration layer that surfaces only under high concurrency. About The Team You'll join a team of curious, driven engineers who believe that technical excellence and world-class reliability are not aspirations - they are the baseline our customers deserve. If you want to build something that matters, alongside people who challenge and inspire you, this is the place. This is a rare opportunity to design and operate systems at true cloud scale while developing deep expertise across three of the most transformative domains in modern engineering: cloud computing, database technologies, and artificial intelligence. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses. Inclusive Team Culture AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role:

We're hiring several Product Operations Managers to embed within our core product teams. Each will contribute to a key component of our stack. Whether you are ensuring models work within each of our harnesses, prioritizing a great experience across cloud offerings, or building the application layer that keeps users on the frontier, the Product Operations team is an integral part of delivering great products to the world. 

Product Operations is the connective tissue between Research, Product, and the market. We shorten the distance between what our models can do and what people get to use. Each of us sits inside one product team as an extension of its leadership, and together we run one shared operating system for how Anthropic ships and learns.

On a given day you might get a launch through its final review, run an early access window, or triaging customer feedback. The rest of the week you build the systems so the team ships and learns faster next time. Our team is small and gets unusual leverage from Claude enabling us to fill gaps across the company and deliver outsized value.

Responsibilities:

1. Ship with confidence

  • Own launch readiness for your team. Keep our launch calendar the source of truth for what is shipping and when.
  • Get every major launch through go/no-go: pre-read written, Security, Safeguards, Legal, and Commercial sign-offs recorded, and any accepted risk written down on purpose.
  • Run early access and beta programs that return signal Product and Research can act on. Define the question before the window opens, give testers the scaffolding to answer it, and close each one with a retro on whether the feedback landed.
  • Program manage new model launches on your surface: readiness goals set in advance, testing and eval coverage tracked, issues triaged, prompting changes landed, retro run. You won't write the evals. You run the program around them.

2. Close the loop with users

  • Turn a lot of noise into two clear signals: what users are asking for, ranked by impact and mapped to the roadmap, and which customers or cohorts are blocked, on what, and why it matters.
  • Plug your team into Anthropic's shared feedback systems rather than building a private one, and improve the shared systems where they fall short.
  • Make sure the field, Support, and Research hear back about what happened with what they sent.

3. Run the team's operating system

  • Set the team's pace: planning, business and execution reviews, goal tracking, offsites.
  • Own how your team works with Legal, Safeguards, Security, GTM, and other product teams so partnering with your team is predictable.
  • Push reporting overhead toward zero. Reviews and digests should be generated from data that already exists.
  • Fill the gaps. Every embedded seat carries one or two projects unique to its team, for example managing Monthly Business Reviews and helping track progress between cycles.

4. Build with Claude

  • Build the tools you need yourself: Claude-powered triage, dashboards that read and write to our systems of record, skills and agents that take the chasing out of the job.
  • Contribute what you build back to the ProdOps team as reusable patterns (launch checklists, EAP setup, lookbacks, deprecations) so nobody starts from scratch.

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • Have owned an operational program end to end (launches, early access, feedback, or planning) that a product team relied on to make decisions. You designed it and ran it, not just executed someone else's plan.
  • Have built a process from zero to one and then simplified it as it scaled. You treat process as a product: it has users, metrics, and a happy path people want to follow.
  • Have worked embedded with product leadership and can move a team without formal authority.
  • Build with AI yourself. You have shipped Claude or other LLM-powered workflows, written the prompts, iterated on the outputs, and can describe model behavior with specifics.
  • Have direct experience managing evals, refining system prompts, and adapting harnesses to new models. 
  • Have direct experience working with Cloud providers in partnership or GTM capacity
  • Have commitment to safe deployment of AI. Bonus if experience with AI Safety and Safeguards.

Bonus:

  • Program managed model launches or model quality at an application-layer AI product.
  • Run early access, beta, or design partner programs.
  • Product management, technical program management, chief of staff, or strategy and operations experience at a startup or fast-growing product company.

03aeb96de1089de587ec.description: LOCATION: CALMSDEN, CIRENCESTER, UK. LIMITED FIELD TRAVEL AS REQUIRED | 5 DAYS ONSITE     THE LAST FRONTIER   ARD was founded on a paradox. The Arctic is both the next great economic frontier and one of the most hostile environments on Earth. Rich in resources and strategically vital, yet bone-chillingly cold, dark for months, and fundamentally inhospitable to humans. This paradox - an explosion of activity in a place that resists human presence - is why we exist.    Our solution is autonomy.    We build systems that operate reliably and intelligently in the Arctic, so that humans don't always have to.  Founded by record-holding pioneers with decades of polar experience, we take calculated risks on hard problems that matter. If you want to build and deploy ground-up technology with real-world impact, at an inflection point in history that won’t reappear, we’d like to talk.     THE ROLE     ARD is growing and we’re looking for an  Assembly and Test Technician  to help us build and test our ruggedized hardware - from field-ready energy and battery systems to the autonomous platforms we deploy in the Arctic. Right now, our biggest constraint isn’t design. It’s the time it takes to assemble and test what we’ve designed.  Reporting to our  Senior Test Engineer , you’ll join our engineering team, working alongside our mechanical and electrical engineers and across our main hardware workstreams. You’ll take hands-on ownership of assembly and testing, helping with the practical implementation and testing of engineering designs. Within your first 3 months, you’ll have helped to take assembly and test off the critical path on our key projects, and helped put in place the documentation and test processes that let us build and test consistently, unit after unit.    CORE RESPONSIBILITIES     Assemble mechanical and electrical sub-assemblies, harnesses, PCBAs,  and complete units to drawings and build instructions, so they’re ready for test on schedule.    Run test phases on assemblies and finished units and record the results accurately, so issues are found and fixed before hardware reaches the field.    Help set up repeatable test processes, from test plans and rigs to how results are captured, working closely with our Senior Test Engineer.    Write and maintain build instructions, test procedures and records, raising the standard of our engineering documentation as we scale.    Spot and report problems found during build and test, giving engineers the detail they need to debug and improve the next design revision.       REQUIREMENTS      About You    You’re a practical, hands-on technician who takes pride in building things properly and getting the details right. You’re methodical, you like a clear process, and you’d rather write something down than rely on memory. You might come from a technician role in engineering, manufacturing or a test lab, an engineering apprenticeship, the armed forces, or a mechanical or electrical engineering degree with plenty of hands-on build experience.    *  Please note: this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship  *     Essential     An engineering qualification (such as an HNC/HND, apprenticeship or degree in mechanical or electrical engineering), or equivalent hands-on experience.    Hands-on experience assembling mechanical or electrical hardware in a workshop, lab or production setting.    Experience with basic soldering equipment    Ability to work from engineering drawings, schematics and written build instructions.    Experience running tests on hardware and recording the results accurately.    Confident using common workshop tools and electrical test equipment, such as multimeters and bench power supplies.    Comfortable owning your own tasks with guidance from the engineering team, and raising problems early when a build or test doesn’t go to plan.       Desirable     Experience writing or improving build instructions, test procedures or other technical documentation.    Experience with electrical assembly such as wiring looms, crimping or soldering, or working with battery systems.    Experience building hardware in small batches or repeat runs, rather than one-off prototypes.    Experience with surface-mount PCB assembly       Future Security Clearance Requirements     As our business scales into the defence and security sectors, the responsibilities of this role are expected to evolve to include projects requiring  UK Security Check (SC) clearance .    While an active clearance is not required to apply or start in this role, candidates must be willing and eligible to undergo UK Government security vetting in the future should project requirements dictate it.    To meet the standard eligibility criteria for UK standard SC vetting, you must typically have resided in the UK for the  past 5 continuous years , hold a valid passport, and be capable of passing comprehensive background, financial, and criminal record checks.       Why ARD      The mission  - The Arctic is the fastest-changing region on Earth. You'll build the intelligence layer that helps understand and steward it — an early-warning system for the planet's coldest edge.   Early stage, real influence  - ARD is at an exciting early stage. You'll join while our products, team and culture are still taking shape, and your ideas will directly influence where we go next.   Ownership and accountability  - We give people real responsibility from day one. You'll own your work end to end, be trusted to make decisions, and be accountable for delivering results that ship and get used.   A small but growing team  - You'll work closely with experienced colleagues across science, software and hardware, with no layers in between. As we grow, you'll help build the team and the ways of working that come next.     WHAT WE OFFER     Competitive compensation    Private Health Insurance from Day 1    Dental & Vision    Equity - meaningful options as an early employee at an early-stage company    Real field exposure - travel to Arctic sites and Outposts when needed    Mission-driven culture - focus on impact, not hours logged      ARD is an equal opportunities employer. We hire on merit, based on skills, experience and potential, and welcome applications from everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. We know great candidates sometimes hold back unless they tick every box, so if this role excites you but your experience doesn’t match every point, we’d still love to hear from you, especially if you bring a background or perspective that is under-represented in science and engineering.  If you need any adjustments during the application or interview process, please don't hesitate to let us know at    #LI-TK1  Find more  English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Reinforcement learning (RL) is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. This role sits on the team that builds and owns the RL training system: the system that trains our production models and that researchers across Anthropic run their experiments on. The team works closely with research teams across the company on the science and engineering of making RL work at scale.

As a Research Engineer on the team, you'll work at the center of RL at Anthropic. You'll have a direct view of how RL training behaves at the frontier because the system you own sits underneath both production and research runs. You will use it with collaborators across research teams to understand what is working, what is fragile, and where the next improvements are.

Key responsibilities

  • Build, own, and improve the core RL training system that serves Anthropic's production and research runs
  • Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference, evaluation) wherever the system needs it
  • Study how RL training behaves at scale and contribute to the research that improves it, in collaboration with teams across Anthropic
  • Implement new training methods as stable, fast, well-tested code
  • Improve the speed and efficiency of RL training and evaluation through profiling, optimization, and benchmarking
  • Make the system easier for researchers to build on, through clean abstractions, clear APIs, and automated testing
  • Debug hard problems across the stack, from a run that has quietly drifted to a distributed systems failure that only shows up at scale
  • Communicate results clearly, in writing and in discussion

Minimum qualifications

  • Proficiency in Python and experience working in, debugging, and improving a large ML codebase
  • Experience with large-scale machine learning training (reinforcement learning, pretraining, or post-training) or the systems that support it
  • Experience with at least one modern ML framework (JAX, PyTorch, or similar)
  • Ability to design controlled experiments and reach conclusions you and others can trust
  • Ability to balance research exploration with engineering implementation
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Care about the societal impacts of your work and are committed to developing safe and beneficial systems

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with reinforcement learning for large language models, in research, production, or both
  • Experience studying training at scale: scaling behavior, training dynamics, or method development on large models
  • Experience with large-scale distributed training systems
  • Familiarity with LLM architectures and training methodologies
  • Experience working close to a frontier training run
  • Experience profiling and optimizing the performance of ML workloads
  • Experience with RL environments, evaluations, or sandboxed code execution
  • Experience with Rust or C++
  • Enjoy pair programming (we love to pair!)

Back to jobs Business Systems Analyst, New Product Introduction San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA Apply About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We launch new products, models and pricing often, and each launch has to work in our systems on day one. A seller needs to be able to quote it, Deal Desk needs to be able to approve it, billing needs to charge for it correctly, and Finance needs to report on it. This role owns how a launch gets into our quote-to-cash systems, from the first pricing conversation to the first invoice. We are looking for someone who treats every launch as a change across many systems. You will join launch planning early, work out what has to change across catalog, quoting, contracts, billing, tax and reporting, and get all of it ready before the launch date. You will build a good part of the Salesforce work yourself and partner with our Salesforce developers and Billing Engineering on the rest. You will be the named owner of the NPI process for systems, and the person Product, Pricing and Finance call when they want to know what it takes to launch something. We are an AI-first systems team. You will use Claude as a normal part of how you design, build, test and document, and you will look for ways to make launches faster and more repeatable with AI. Key responsibilities Own the systems side of new product and pricing launches, from the first pricing discussion through launch day and the first billing cycle Turn a pricing and packaging decision into concrete system changes: SKUs, price books, bundles, discount and approval rules, contract terms, billing plans, tax codes and reporting Build and run a repeatable NPI playbook: intake, a readiness checklist, sign-offs, a launch calendar and a post-launch review Join launch planning early with Product and Pricing. Push back on pricing ideas that cannot be quoted, billed or reported cleanly, and offer options that can Design how new pricing models work end to end, including usage-based, seat-based, tiered, committed and multi-year ramp pricing, and which system is the source of truth for each part Plan the impact on existing customers: moving customers to new SKUs, grandfathering, amendments and co-termination, and how renewals will work Own end-of-sale and retirement of products and prices, so old SKUs leave the catalog without breaking renewals, billing or reporting Coordinate the changes across Salesforce, billing and our tax platform, working with the teams who own each system Partner with Deal Desk, Sales, Finance, Accounting, Tax and Legal so each team signs off on what changes for them before launch Make sure sellers and Deal Desk are ready on launch day, including quote templates, approval paths, guidance and enablement Check every launch after it goes live: do quotes, orders, invoices and Finance reports match? Add the control or reconciliation that catches the gaps Build and ship declarative solutions yourself where that is the right call, and write specs clear enough that developers can build the rest without several rounds of questions Use AI to shorten launch cycles, for example generating catalog changes from a pricing spec, checking launch readiness, and testing quote and billing scenarios Minimum qualifications Experience in GTM or revenue systems as a Business Systems Analyst, Q2C Systems Lead or similar role, with hands-on ownership of product and pricing launches Experience launching new products or pricing models at a fast-growing company, owning the change across catalog, quoting, contracts and billing Hands-on experience with Salesforce CPQ, Revenue Cloud or a similar CPQ tool, especially product and pricing data models, price books, bundles and approval rules Working understanding of how a pricing decision flows into bookings, invoicing, tax and revenue recognition Experience running a cross-functional process with many sign-offs (Product, Finance, Legal, Sales) and getting to launch on a fixed date Hands-on Salesforce admin skills (Flow, validation rules, page layouts, approval processes) and comfort building meaningful parts of your own solution Clear communication across Product, sellers, Deal Desk, Finance, Legal and engineers, adjusting the level of detail for each Preferred qualifications Experience in GTM, revenue or finance systems roles Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing, and with billing platforms such as Stripe, Metronome or Zuora Experience moving existing customers onto new pricing, including migrations, grandfathering and amendments at scale Experience with tax setup for new products (tax codes, tax engines such as Anrok or Avalara) Experience with integrations between Salesforce and billing, ERP or provisioning systems, and comfort reading API payloads and integration logs Basic SQL and comfort using a data warehouse to check launch data Salesforce Administrator certification. CPQ Specialist, Advanced Administrator or Business Analyst certification is a plus Hands-on use of AI tools (Claude or similar) in how you design, build or document systems, and the ability to explain how you check their output The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $270,000 - $315,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. 07096f36a733430e2b64.description: Scrum Master – Mobile Products About the Role We are seeking a proactive Scrum Master with experience supporting mobile product teams. You will guide Agile delivery, improve team effectiveness and work closely with the Product Owner, developers, QA teams, stakeholders and customers to deliver measurable business results. Key Responsibilities Facilitate Scrum ceremonies, including sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews and retrospectives. Coach teams and stakeholders on Agile principles and Scrum practices, encouraging collaboration and continuous improvement. Identify and remove impediments, manage dependencies and help the team maintain a sustainable delivery pace. Support the Product Owner with backlog refinement, clear user stories, acceptance criteria and effective prioritisation. Help translate product roadmap priorities into achievable sprint goals. Collaborate with developers, QA teams and stakeholders to improve delivery quality and predictability. Support customer engagement and ensure feedback informs delivery and product improvements. Use delivery metrics, product analytics and customer insights to guide improvements and measure results. Proactively identify opportunities to reduce costs, improve efficiency and support revenue growth. Explore practical uses of AI to improve team processes, reporting and delivery. Skills & Experience Proven experience as a Scrum Master, Product Owner or Agile Delivery Lead. Strong knowledge of Agile principles and practical experience applying Scrum. Experience working with mobile applications, devices or technologies, ideally across iOS and Android. Strong facilitation, coaching and conflict-resolution skills. Experience supporting backlog management, sprint planning and refinement. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work across technical teams, business stakeholders and customers. A proactive approach to resolving blockers and driving improvements through to completion. Evidence of successful delivery outcomes, supported by measurable improvements in quality, efficiency or business performance. Experience using data to inform decisions and improve team effectiveness. Scrum certification and practical experience with AI tools are desirable.

076263eef95ffa899e7b.description: About Pleo   Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.  The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.  Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.   About the role    Pleo's Intelligence function covers the full analytical picture - product behaviour, GTM performance, commercial data science, financial reporting, and operational intelligence. The Analytics Engineers who serve these teams own the data modelling layer that all of it runs on: dbt models, metric definitions, and semantic layer contributions that analysts, product teams, and AI tools depend on to get consistent, trustworthy answers.  You'll be embedded in the Product Intelligence team, building the tracking, experimentation, and data modelling foundations that make product data trustworthy and self-serve. You'll join a close-knit team actively migrating our analytics stack onto a new Analytics Warehouse and Omni, moving off legacy tools like Looker and Hippocampus. If you want to build the infrastructure that other people's product decisions run on rather than just report on what exists, this is the opportunity for you.    Who you'll work with and reporting to    You will report to an Analytics Manager leading Product Intelligence and Growth Intelligence. You'll partner closely with Product Managers, Product Analysts, and Engineering to get tracking, experimentation, and metric definitions right from the ground up. You'll also engage with the broader Analytics Engineering community across Pleo to drive shared standards, especially around the semantic layer that keeps metrics consistent across the organization.    What you'll be doing     Build and maintain dbt models in our new Analytics Warehouse, using a clean, layered architecture and migrating logic off legacy tools as you go.    Own tracking plan implementation and QA directly in Segment and Amplitude in close partnership with Product and Engineering. 076f7518ff1470f88e5a.description: At Bending Spoons, we’re striving to build one of the all-time great companies. A company that serves a huge number of customers. A company where team members grow to their full potential. A company that functions at unparalleled levels of effectiveness and efficiency. A company that creates value for shareowners at an extraordinary rate. And a company that does so while adhering to high ethical standards. In pursuit of this objective, we acquire and improve digital businesses, not to sell on, but to own and operate for the long term. The transformations we make are often deep—designed to speed up innovation, benefit customers, and strengthen business performance. Here, hierarchy is minimal and teams are small and talent-dense. We operate established products with the ambition, agility, and urgency of a startup. Across the company, we integrate AI deeply into how we work so that human judgment and machine intelligence reinforce each other. For a talented, driven, and collaborative individual, working at Bending Spoons is an opportunity to learn, make an impact, and progress their career at an exceptionally high rate. That’s our promise to such a candidate. A few examples of your responsibilities Shape the B2B sales function. Joining a fast-moving team building a world-class B2B sales function, you’ll help define the strategy, approach, and guiding principles that set a new standard for excellence in enterprise sales. Curate high-potential leads. Build a portfolio of revenue-driving corporate clients, leveraging the latest AI tools to prioritize where you invest your time for long-term growth. Learn the industry inside and out. Understand the incentives, pressure points, and decision-makers of your industry so you can build powerful, profitable relationships. Be a credible voice for the product. Speak about it with clarity and confidence. Gather feedback from clients and share insights to help shape future development. Follow the data. Keep a close eye on performance metrics to gauge impact and zero in on the highest-value actions and opportunities. Stand out at every touchpoint. Deliver outstanding service that builds trust with every client interaction. What we look for Reasoning ability. Given the necessary knowledge, you can solve complex problems. You think from first principles, and structure your ideas sharply. You resist the influence of biases. You identify and take care of the details that matter. Drive. You’re extremely ambitious in everything you do—and your initiative, effort, and tenacity match the intensity of your ambition. You feel deeply responsible for your work. You hold yourself to a high—and rising—bar. Team spirit. You give generously and without the expectation of receiving in return. You support the best idea, not your idea. You're always happy to get your hands dirty to help your team. You’re reliable, honest, and transparent. Proficiency in English. You read, write, and speak proficiently in English. What we offer Incredibly talented, entrepreneurial teams. You’ll work in small, result-oriented, autonomous teams alongside some of the brightest people in your field. An exceptional opportunity for growth. We go to great lengths to hire individuals of outstanding potential—then, our priority is to put them in the ideal position to thrive. Spooners in their 20s lead products worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And if you’ve got what it takes, you’ll soon be playing an essential role in major projects, too. All. These. Benefits. Flexible hours, remote working, unlimited backing for learning and training, top-of-the-market health insurance, a rich relocation package, generous parental support, and a yearly retreat to a stunning location. We help each Spooner set up the conditions to do their best work. Competitive pay and access to company equity at a discount. Typical annual salary offers range from £68,579 to £112,189 in London and from €54,346 to €82,557 elsewhere in Europe. The lower end of these ranges applies to candidates with little or no relevant experience, while exceptionally experienced candidates may receive offers of up to £316,052 in London or €240,330 elsewhere in Europe. Candidates offered a permanent contract may choose to receive part of their compensation in discounted company equity. Commitment & contract Permanent or fixed-term. Full-time or part-time. Location Milan (Italy), London (UK), Madrid (Spain), Warsaw (Poland), or fully remote from eligible countries. The selection process In our screening process, we prioritize verifiable signals of excellence, regardless of seniority. There are no preferential paths beyond what your application demonstrates, and we evaluate every candidate through the same process. Some people hold back because they feel they lack experience or have an “imperfect” CV. If you like the role and believe you could excel over time, don’t self-reject. All applications go through our careers page, which is the only way to be considered. If you pass our screening, you’ll be asked to complete one or more tests. They are challenging, may involve unfamiliar problems, and can take several hours. To learn more about what to expect throughout the selection process, you can find additional information here. We set the bar high and won’t extend an offer until we’re confident we’ve found the right candidate. This is why a job may remain open for months or be reposted several times. We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form. Before you apply If you’ve applied before but didn't receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again. Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. While this tends to lead to extraordinary learning, achievement, and career growth, it also requires significant commitment. To help you ramp up quickly and set yourself up for success, we expect you to spend most days in our Milan office during your first few months with us, regardless of your long-term work location. It’s the best way to rapidly absorb our company culture and build trust with your new teammates. We’ll support you with generous travel and accommodation assistance. After that, you’re welcome to work from one of our offices, or remotely from approved countries—depending on what we agree at the offer stage. If the role speaks to you and you’re excited to give your best, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now—we can’t wait to meet you.

077d2e6ccbcbb334984d.description: About Us  At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.  We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.  We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.  Read more about what we’re building    here   .     About the role  Software Engineers at Axle build the core infrastructure for connecting to distributed energy devices, orchestrating them, and allowing them to participate in electricity markets.  This is a generalist Software Engineering role, encompassing product-engineering, devops, and data engineering. We encourage engineers to own as much of the problem-space as they can: you’ll spend time talking to clients, getting feedback from users, and working closely with market operators.  At Axle, we work in a deliberately flat structure. That means fewer layers, faster decisions, and more ownership for everyone.    Software engineering at Axle looks like    Forming a deep understanding of the domain & the business, so you have enough context to execute independently at speed    Focusing on outcomes, not process, and taking ownership for the end product you ship into the world    Managing your own time and those of others to adapt to changing scope and deadlines, delivering 80% of the value in 20% of the time      Tech stack  🐍 We build in Python + React for the frontend  🐋 Everything we build lives in Docker, for minimal cross-platform faff and maximal reproducibility. 🤖 Unlimited Claude Code tokens - we are aggressive users and explorers of AI, and encourage everybody to reconsider their workflows regularly  ☁️ We deploy on GCP    What's in it for you  A meaningful slice of equity in Axle, alongside a competitive salary, with total compensation ranging from £75k–£200k (base salary + equity).   We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.  Enhanced parental leave to support you through life's meaningful moments.  Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.  Hybrid working - We have a dog-friendly office around Farringdon. To maximize collaboration, we ask that you spend 2-3 days a week in the office.  The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.    We are  extremely  keen to build a diverse company, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.    Inte

We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role The Endpoint team (Client Platform Engineering) manages the laptops and handsets every Anthropic employee works on, plus the infrastructure underneath them. We treat the fleet as a distributed platform, not a collection of devices, and every piece of configuration ships as code through pull requests, CI, staging, and a canary group. Today the mobile side of the fleet is BYOD. This role exists to change that. You will design and implement a corporate-issued mobile device program (managed company phones and managed Apple accounts) in every region Anthropic operates in, and take it from early design to production. The team is deliberately lean and runs with high autonomy. You’ll define what a corporate mobile program looks like at Anthropic and own the platform decisions that get it there. Responsibilities Design the corporate-issued mobile device program: device standards, what we issue to whom, and how the program grows from a first region to everywhere Anthropic operates Own the global logistics of issuing hardware: procurement partners, regional coverage, spares, and refresh cycles Bring mobile configuration into the team’s config-as-code pipeline so mobile policies are reviewed, tested, and progressively rolled out like the rest of the fleet Build zero-touch enrollment: Apple Business Manager and ADE with managed Apple accounts on iOS, the zero-touch equivalent on Android, so a new phone works the first time without hands-on setup Own policy, compliance, and device lifecycle for the corporate fleet, from issue to wipe Build telemetry on the corporate fleet: which devices are checking in, OS and patch state, drift between reported and actual state Own managed app distribution for mobile, from app approval through update rollout Partner with Corporate Security on device posture, device trust signals, and travel devices for international trips Decide how corporate-issued and BYOD coexist, and own that boundary as the program rolls out You may be a good fit if you Have owned a global or multi-region mobile device program end to end, with 8+ years managing corporate fleets at thousands-of-devices scale Go deep on iOS device management: enrollment flows, Apple Business Manager and ADE, APNs and certificate lifecycle, declarative device management Have worked with Android device management and can hold your own in a mixed fleet Treat device configuration as code and have moved past clicking in consoles Have run the infrastructure under an MDM, not just administered a SaaS console: a self-hosted MDM server, AWS, Terraform, and configuration that ships as code Have built or launched a corporate device program, not just operated one, and can decide how it coexists with BYOD Excel at ambiguous problems that touch several teams at once Communicate technical concepts clearly to any audience View IT Engineering as requiring product engineering rigor Write clear documentation as a natural part of your workflow Strong candidates may also Have managed ChromeOS devices alongside a mobile fleet Have run a device program across multiple regions and dealt with the logistics that come with it Have built automated, progressive rollout systems with promotion gated on telemetry Bring proficiency in Swift for building device tooling Have used LLMs to automate operational work, or are excited to make Claude a teammate Technical Skills Python and shell scripting iOS and Android platform internals (depth on iOS, working knowledge of Android) Modern MDM or UEM platforms (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE, or equivalent) Running the infrastructure under an MDM (self-hosted servers, AWS GCP, Terraform) Querying live device state at fleet scale Mobile device lifecycle automation (enrollment, policy, patching, app distribution) GitOps and CI for configuration management Endpoint security fundamentals Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $285,000 - $325,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
