About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As an Enforcement Lead, you will be responsible for managing and executing enforcement actions across our products and services, with a focus on detecting and mitigating attempts to misuse Anthropic's AI systems for malicious cyber operations. Your work will center on developing strategic enforcement frameworks for flagged activity related to cyberattacks, malware development, and offensive exploitation. Additionally, you will manage a team of Cyber Enforcement Analysts and contractors implementing this enforcement strategy. 

Safety is core to our mission, and you'll help uphold policy enforcement so that our users can safely interact with and build on top of our products in a harmless, helpful, and honest way.

Important context for this role: In this position you may be exposed to and engage with explicit content spanning a range of topics, including those of a violent, technical, or psychologically disturbing nature. This role may require responding to escalations during weekends and holidays.

Key responsibilities

  • Manage a team of Cyber Enforcement Analysts and contractors, overseeing the vision of Cyber Enforcement strategy 

  • Create strategies to detect and mitigate potential misuse of AI systems to facilitate cyberattacks, malware creation, exploitation tooling, and related harmful cyber operations

  • Collaborate with stakeholders regarding novel, ambiguous, or high-severity cases

  • Collaborate with the Safeguards Policy Design Team on policy gaps surfaced through real enforcement scenarios

  • Partner with Engineering and Data Science teams to ensure tooling and measurement support enforcement operations.

  • Keep up to date with emerging AI policy enforcement best practices, threat actor tactics, and the evolving cyber threat landscape, using these to inform enforcement decisions

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience as a people manager

  • Experience in cybersecurity, including knowledge of offensive techniques, exploit development, malware analysis, or vulnerability research

  • Experience performing content review, abuse investigations, or policy enforcement at volume

  • Proficiency in SQL and/or Python for data analysis and threat detection

  • Experience identifying emerging risks and communicating findings to a diverse set of stakeholders, such as Product, Policy, Engineering, and Legal teams

  • Experience working with generative AI products, including writing effective prompts for content review and enforcement

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in trust & safety, abuse investigations, cybersecurity investigations, or threat intelligence in a technology or AI company

  • Experience with large language models and an understanding of how AI technology could be misused for cyber operations

  • Experience operating within abuse monitoring programs or enforcement review systems

  • Understanding of the challenges involved in implementing product policies at scale, including in the content moderation space

  • Experience working with government agencies, regulated environments, or information sharing communities

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$285,000—$330,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

As we continue to expand our global footprint, we're looking for passionate people to join our mission. If you're ready to help the world's best companies optimize their digital applications, we invite you to explore a career with us!

Your Opportunity

Are you looking to take the next step in your sales career? Join New Relic, a leader in observability and application performance monitoring, where you can transition from an inbound-focused role to a key player on our outbound-driven Business Development team. You'll be a key part of our go-to-market strategy, joining a high-energy team that's at the forefront of building our pipeline. We're looking for individuals who are passionate about sales and keen to develop their expertise in an outbound-focused role.
You'll be supported by personalised coaching, world-class tools, and significant opportunities for career growth. At New Relic, hard work is celebrated, teamwork is a core value, and every success is shared. This is a chance to build a lasting sales career with a company that believes in investing in its people.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's go-to-market organization is growing quickly, and our most important priorities for customers and for our field rarely sit within one team. Priorities cut across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product, Revenue Operations, Enablement, Finance, Legal, Partnerships and more. We're looking for a strategic program manager to own these initiatives end to end. 

You'll start with an ambiguous ask, sometimes from a senior leader and sometimes from a signal in the data. You'll find the root cause of the problem and design a solution with subject-matter experts across the company, then drive it from strategy to planning to results to iteration. You’ll bring stakeholders along while still moving quickly to the right answer. The work ranges from large cross-functional programs to short, focused SWAT efforts on urgent questions. Success looks like making better decisions, faster, for our customers and our field.

This is a strategic, highly cross-functional individual contributor role for someone equally comfortable building a business case, running a forum with senior stakeholders, getting into the data, and working directly with the field. You'll operate with high autonomy on the most critical GTM questions we face.

Key responsibilities

  • Own a portfolio of strategic GTM programs end to end, each starting from a business problem (e.g., customer activation, seller efficiency, model launches) and running from scoping through launch, operationalization, results, and iteration
  • Act as a thought partner to Sales and GTM leaders: identify, scope, and prioritize the programs most worth doing, and say no to the rest
  • Turn ambiguous, loosely scoped problems into structured analysis, a defensible model, and a clear plan with owners, milestones, and decision points
  • Align and drive teams across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product, Revenue Operations, Enablement, Finance, Legal, and Partnerships without formal authority over any of them
  • Engage senior executives on the status and outcomes of the most critical programs
  • Manage change so new programs are adopted by the field, and define and report on success metrics such as adoption, time-to-value, and productivity impact
  • Use AI tools every day to analyze, model, and build faster
  • Create the templates, cadence, and reporting that help every future program launch well

Minimum qualifications

  • Have led complex cross-functional programs from problem definition through delivery, in strategy consulting, strategy and operations, GTM or sales programs, or program management
  • A track record of turning ambiguous problems into clear, defensible recommendations
  • Have driven initiatives to completion across teams you do not manage, including when senior stakeholders disagreed
  • Analytical skills: building a business case and quantitative model, defining targets, and pulling and analyzing your own data from CRM and BI tools
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with experience presenting analysis and recommendations to senior and executive audiences
  • A working understanding of how an enterprise sales organization operates
  • Have built programs or processes where none existed, and owned the outcome through to results
  • Are motivated by Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

Preferred qualifications

  • A background in strategy consulting followed by an in-house role where you built and ran programs and strategic projects 
  • Experience running sales or GTM programs with measured results, such as pipeline, activation, adoption, or launch programs
  • Experience working within a sales operating cadence, such as forecast calls and pipeline reviews, Sales planning, product launches 
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools daily to work faster and more rigorously, including building workflows with Claude or similar tools
  • Experience at a company selling technical or AI products
  • Experience as an early hire in a new team or function

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$270,000—$310,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Daarnaast bieden wij je de kans om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen. Je duikt in de wereld van de Cloud en ontwerpt, implementeert en beheert de CI/CD DevOps pipelines. Hoe je dit doet? De diversiteit in werklocaties, welke maximaal één uur van huis liggen, laat je kennismaken met vele organisaties. Zo blijf je ontwikkelen binnen jouw vakgebied. CI/CD en Release Engineering tooling en praktijken Containerisatie en Orchestratie. SRE-praktijken en principes In bezit van een rijbewijs Soft Skills: Uitstekende probleemoplossende en analytische vaardigheden Sterke communicatieve en samenwerkingsvaardigheden Vermogen om zelfstandig te werken en meerdere taken tegelijk te beheren. Solliciteer via onze website naar deze vacature DevOps Engineer in Amsterdam of Rotterdam. Als je betaalt in de winkel. Als je een glas kraanwater drinkt. Als je een paspoort aanvraagt. 0d7caf63613ce698f971.description: We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from diverse backgrounds, including consumer tech, finance and media, and companies like Dyson, Shopify, Meta and Tesla. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you'll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural, alongside other renowned investors. Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house, hardware and software. Our work involves building robots in our workshop and houses on real construction sites, so we're onsite five days a week. Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company . You might enjoy our YouTube Channel , Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage , or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like . About the role You’ll transport robots that build houses. You’ll load them at our Amsterdam workshop, get them onto construction sites, and bring them back for repairs before their next job. When a team needs a replacement robot to keep building, you’re the person who gets it there. We’re hiring our first Robot Transporter. We already have 150+ robots in the field and we’re expanding from the Netherlands into the UK and US. You’ll be the first person dedicated to getting our robots, equipment and materials where they need to be, helping more teams build more homes. Your day could take you from the workshop to several active construction sites, delivering robots, collecting systems for repair and getting equipment to the next crew. You’ll work out the order of stops, what fits in each vehicle, and how to load and secure it safely. You’ll drive a C-licence box truck or B-licence van, work closely with our deployment team, and get to know the robots and the people building with them. This is practical, physical work with room to take charge. You’ll start by planning alongside the deployment team, then take ownership of routes and transport requests as you learn the sites and loads. Plans change, sites get muddy, and teams depend on you. You’ll see the houses going up and know you helped get them built. What you'll do Drive. Operate our leased C-licence box truck and our B-licence van across the Netherlands, usually two or more movements a day. When a move needs a flatbed with forklift loading, you arrange it. Plan the day’s transport. Work with the deployment team on the day’s plan: what goes in which vehicle, and the order of drop-offs and pick-ups across sites, our Groningen hub and our Amsterdam locations. Over time, more of this becomes yours to own. Load and secure. Robots, hoisting cages, scaffolding, inventory kits, equipment. You know weight limits, lashing and what it takes to get a 400+ kg system in and out of a vehicle safely. Run deployment logistics. Systems, kits and operational tools out to a new site before the team arrives, back to the workshop when a build wraps, and everything in between. Keep the fleet where it's useful. Move idle systems from one site to another that needs them, and bring systems back for repair so that a broken robot swapped today is a wall going up tomorrow. Own the vehicles. Servicing, inspections, cleaning, fuel, damage reporting and fines. Vehicles are always road-ready. Log every move. Each transport is recorded in our fleet tooling so deployment managers see when their request is planned and the company always knows where every system and kit is. Improve the process. Feed what you see on the road back to the inventory team (packing standards), deployment team (equipment ratios per site) and the team building our transport tooling. Help with inventory in downtime. When there's nothing to move, you work with the inventory team to prepare kits, organise stock and check returned equipment back in. What we're looking for A valid C licence with Code 95 and a driver card (bestuurderskaart) (required). Professional driving and load securing experience (required). Trucks, ideally box trucks with tail lift, with real responsibility for what was in the back: lashing, weight distribution, awkward loads. Equipment rental, construction logistics, removals or last-mile delivery are all good backgrounds. Comfortable with physical work. Loading heavy systems with the right equipment, early starts, all weather, construction site conditions. You don’t need a robotics or construction background, but you should want to know how the systems you’re moving work. Organised in chaos. You can hold a day with five drop-offs in your head, re-sequence it when a site calls, and still log everything at the end. Reliable and careful. A damaged robot costs a build day. You check straps twice and say no to an overloaded vehicle. Clear communication. You deal with deployment managers, site crews and the workshop every day, in person and on Slack. You raise problems early. Based in the Netherlands. Able to work from Amsterdam and drive to sites nationwide. We can't support relocation or visa sponsorship for this role. English required; Dutch is a plus. Nice to have Forklift certificate (heftruckcertificaat) VCA safety certificate (we can arrange it) Basic mechanical sense: you notice when something on a vehicle or a system doesn't look right Experience planning for more than one driver or vehicle Comfortable with simple apps and forms for logging work Why Monumental? Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. If you're driven by innovation, eager to tackle complex challenges, and ready to make a tangible difference, we want to hear from you. For open applications (where you don't see an exact role match), please reach out to us at: iwanttojoin@monumental.co - share with us the most interesting or challenging project you've worked on, why you want to join and your CV or portfolio. Unfortunately we do not currently support internships. If you don't meet all the qualifications here but are excited about Monumental and feel you'd still be able to help us tackle complex challenges, do get in touch. We welcome generalists who focus on outcomes and are eager to learn on the job.

0d964ed67733584995c1.description: Job title: Product Manager - Device Data Management (Fluent French & English) Location: Paris — Hybrid (3 days in office) Salary: €57,600 - €72,000 Team: Product Management - Data Device Management Reporting to: Group Product Manager This role is based in Paris, France and requires the successful candidate to be based in or willing to relocate to Paris. Fluent French and English (spoken and written) are essential for this position. At this time, we are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role. We are committed to building a diverse, global team and our sponsorship policy is evaluated on a role-by-role basis. We encourage you to keep an eye on our careers site to stay informed about future opportunities where we are able to offer visa sponsorship Please submit your profile in English. Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today's challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future. Leveraging Data, AI, and real-time decision-making we turn energy complexity into growth opportunities for our partners. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable and affordable. With teams across Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen. You'll lead the French localisation of Device Data Management — one of the core product areas within the Kaluza platform that brings together data on supplies, meters, registers, reads and consumption. This area also covers the journeys around managing this data (like updating a meter's configuration), the APIs that expose it, the frontend pages that surface it to users, and the calculations behind consumption projection and forecasting. This is a hands-on, full-stack product role — you'll work across the whole product area, from the data model through to what users see on screen. Translate French market requirements into clear specifications — turn the rules of the French energy market (including how device and meter data flows between grid operators and suppliers) into detailed product requirements covering compliance, data flows and data quality. Build close working relationships — work hand in hand with key partners in the French market to understand their needs, shape requirements together, and build the kind of trusted relationship where they come to you first, using that closeness to steer what we build next for France. Build, don't just specify. Go from idea to working prototype yourself — query data, sketch API contracts, and stand up proofs of concept. We expect you to use AI tooling (e.g. Claude Code) as a daily multiplier to prototype, investigate, and unblock, not just to draft documents. Align global and local teams across all functions — partner closely with engineering, UX, QA and more, with full-stack influence, keeping everyone pointed at the right outcomes. Be the go-to person for this product area in France, and act as the link between our global and local teams to inform priorities and strategy. About You Ideally you'll have/be: Proven experience as a Product Manager, Business Analyst, or equivalent role in software companies, with a strong track record of successfully localising complex software products for international markets Previous experience in the French energy industry — you know how the market works and its key players (e.g. Enedis / GRDF), especially around device data and market flows. Experience with energy management or utility platforms in the French market is a strong plus. Fluent in French and very comfortable in English — our platform and many of our teams operate in English, so you move easily between both. Confident working directly with clients — you can run a working session with client stakeholders, draw out the real requirement behind the ask, and keep senior people aligned and brought in. A builder's mentality — resourceful and hands-on, comfortable building a working prototype rather than waiting for the perfect specification. Technically comfortable — at ease with data and data models, databases, and APIs, and able to prototype with modern AI tooling. You don't need to be an engineer, but you think like one and can hold your own in a technical conversation. Equally happy reasoning about a data model and about what the end user sees on screen. A clear, sharp communicator — able to cut through noise and articulate technical and market complexity to a range of stakeholders, including clients. Experience collaborating across cross-functional teams — engineering, QA, BA, Programme, Delivery etc — to deliver localised solutions. Proficiency in AI tools throughout all stages of the product lifecycle — from discovery and ideation to delivery and iteration. Kaluza Values Here at Kaluza we have five core values that guide us as a business: Play to win, Solve the real problem, Build trust every day, Own the outcome, Go further together We want the best people We’re keen to meet people from all walks of life — our view is that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We want to build teams which represent a variety of experiences, perspectives and skills, and we recognise talent on the basis of merit and potential. We understand some people may not apply for jobs unless they tick every box. But if you're excited about joining us and think you have some of what we're looking for, even if you're not 100% sure, we'd still love to hear from you. Find out more about working at Kaluza on our careers page and LinkedIn . You can also find our Applicant Data Protection Policy here .

0f06f4bf393354c94fb9.description: Role Overview We are hiring Graduate Mobile Software Engineers to join NETGEAR's Mobile Engineering team in Cork. You'll help build the next generation of native mobile apps that connect millions of customers to their NETGEAR devices. You'll work alongside experienced mobile engineers across the full product lifecycle, from requirements through build and test to release and the production data that follows. You'll write production code in your first weeks, not your first year, and you'll use AI coding agents as a standard part of your toolkit. Engineers here own their work end to end, including quality; that ownership is the fastest way to earn trust and take on bigger work. What You Will Be Doing Building features in our native Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift) applications, from ticket to release. Owning the quality of what you build, including functional QA, regression testing, and release validation. Testing on real devices to make sure setup flows, error states, and edge cases work for the person holding the phone, not just for the test suite. Writing and maintaining automated unit, integration, and UI tests, so the same bug is never found twice by hand. Working AI-first, using agentic coding tools to plan, write, test, review, and refactor, and helping the team get better at it. Automating repetitive work by contributing to CI/CD pipelines, build tooling, and release automation. Debugging and optimizing using crash, performance, and analytics data from production. Integrating APIs, SDKs, and cloud services to power app functionality. Taking part in agile ceremonies and code reviews, giving and receiving feedback. Doing what the release needs, whether that is a test pass, a build fix, a script, or a spec. What You Will Gain Hands-on experience building and shipping native Android and iOS apps used by millions of customers worldwide. Real ownership of quality, which is the fastest route to trust and scope on this team. A deep understanding of mobile architectures, UI frameworks, and platform APIs. Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and modern DevOps practice. Fluency in AI-assisted development using Claude Code, Copilot, and ChatGPT. A structured graduate onboarding path with a named mentor and a defined first-year development plan. Room to grow within NETGEAR's global engineering organization. What We Are Looking For A Level 8 honours degree (or an equivalent honours bachelor's degree) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronic Engineering, or a related discipline. Real evidence that you can code, in any language. College projects, internships, personal apps, open-source, and hackathons all count. An eye for quality. You notice when something feels wrong for the user, not just when a test fails. Curiosity about AI-assisted development and a willingness to work in a toolchain that is changing quickly. A hands-on attitude. Our best engineers pick up whatever the release needs rather than waiting for it to be assigned. Clear written and spoken communication. Strong problem-solving, attention to detail, and a collaborative mindset. Nice to Have Native mobile experience, Kotlin and Jetpack Compose on Android, or Swift and SwiftUI on iOS. Any published app, even a small one. Experience with cross-platform frameworks such as React Native or Flutter. Exposure to Git, CI/CD, or automated testing. Knowledge of REST APIs and mobile architecture fundamentals such as MVC or MVVM. Interest in networked applications, IoT, or connected devices. We assess aptitude, not a checklist. If you have shipped something you are proud of in any stack, apply. With several roles available, we encourage you to apply even if you don't tick every box. Why Join NETGEAR Build mobile apps that help millions of users manage and connect their devices worldwide. Start your career alongside a Cork-based team that values innovation, craftsmanship, and continuous learning. Work on mobile and IoT technology at a global scale. Learn and deliver faster with leading AI development tools. Competitive salary, pension, healthcare, and share scheme. Key Details Start date: November 2026 Closing date: 1st November 2026 Eligibility to live and work in Ireland is required. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for these roles. Company Statement/Values At NETGEAR, we are on a mission to unleash the full potential of connectivity with intelligent solutions that delight and protect. We turn ideas into innovative networking products that connect people, power businesses, and advance the way we live. We're a performance-driven, talented, and connected team committed to delivering world-class products for our customers. As a company, we value our employees as the most essential building blocks of our success. And as teammates, we commit to taking our work to the Next Gear by living our values: we Dare to Transform the future, Connect and Delight our customers, Communicate Courageously with each other and collaborate to Win It Together . You'll find our values woven through our processes, present in our decisions, and celebrated throughout our culture. We strive to attract top talent and create a great workplace where people feel engaged, inspired, challenged, proud, and respected. If you are creative, forward-thinking, passionate about technology, and looking for a rewarding career to make an impact, then you've got what it takes to succeed at NETGEAR. Join our network and help us shape the future of connectivity. NETGEAR hires based on merit. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

0f17d621dcd3218e5564.description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.    We want you as a highly skilled and experienced  AIT Electrical Engineer  to help us in our mission by leading the design, commissioning, and debugging of electrical systems for various propulsion test benches, as well as testing of engine electrical systems. This is a dynamic, hands-on engineering position that combines systems-level thinking with practical implementation, demanding both deep technical expertise and the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.      Key responsibilities:   In your capacity as an AIT Electrical Engineer, your role will be continuously evolving and often diverse, but day to day your duties will include:    Contribute to the design and development of electrical systems and architecture for test benches, including power distribution, signal conditioning, and control systems.     Lead assembly, integration and testing of electrical components for turbomachinery and engines.    Define test procedures, document results and trace non-conformities    Specify and review electrical schematics, panel layouts, and wiring diagrams to ensure system integrity and compliance with industry standards.     Collaborate with the team to integrate sensors, actuators, power supplies, and DAQ systems.     Conduct system-level troubleshooting and debugging, using advanced diagnostic tools (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, DMMs).     Perform root cause analysis and implement engineering solutions to improve system robustness and reliability.     Provide technical leadership during assembly, commissioning, and test operations.    Document all designs, test results, and configuration changes; contribute to standard operating procedures and risk assessments.    Ensure all electrical systems comply with safety and regulatory standards.      Qualifications:     Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related technical field.     2+ years of experience in electrical engineering, preferably in an aerospace environment      What we would love to see from you:     Strong understanding of electrical design principles, system integration, and instrumentation.    Experience with high voltage systems (200V - 1000V, AC/DC).    Comfortable working hands-on with electrical hardware, wiring, test equipment and instrumentation.    Proven experience designing and commissioning electrical systems, and with testing of electrical systems (e.g. electrical motors and batteries)    Hands-on experience with cabling and harness manufacturing    Proficiency in using common electrical test equipment and CAD tools (e.g., EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical).    Experience with industrial control, automation or data-acquisition systems (e.g. Beckhoff).    Knowledge of electrical standards and best practices for high-reliability applications    Familiarity with test bench operations would be a plus    Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment with a hands-on approach.     Fluency in English, both written and verbal.    A passion for space exploration and a mindset focused on innovation, precision, and safety.       Why you should join us!   What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:      We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind     We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them      We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?      We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.     The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable.       All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. 0f1b6907ef994630f3bc.description: About Stream Stream powers real-time Chat , Video , Activity Feeds , and AI Moderation for more than 1 billion end users across 4,000+ apps, from Strava and Bumble to eBay and Patreon. Our platform processes billions of API requests per month and supports applications with millions of concurrent users, while delivering highly reliable, low-latency services and a great developer experience. The role We're looking for a Staff Backend Engineer to join Stream on our mission of elevating the quality of apps for billions of users globally. You'll own the technical direction of Stream Video's media plane and the infrastructure it runs on. This is a full-time role, hybrid with 3 days a week in our Amsterdam office, or remote from anywhere in the EU. What you'll work on Stream Video runs on an SFU we built in Go on top of Pion, plus ingest and recording fleets, all on a global edge network we own across more than one cloud. Nobody at Stream has owned this media plane end to end before. Our central infrastructure team is tuned for request-based services, and video breaks in different ways: live sessions can't be dropped, bandwidth is the biggest cost, and placement is the main lever. That's why this is a Staff role. You'll set the direction for the video backend and its infrastructure with your own roadmap, reporting to our Director of Engineering with a direct line to our CTO. The Video SDK teams own the client side, and you'll work closely with them and with infrastructure. Part of the fleet is mid-move to Kubernetes. Job responsibilities: Architecture: write the architecture and roadmap for Stream Video's backend and media infrastructure, and decide what ships. Scale livestreaming: architect the SFU and media pipeline (WHIP, WHEP, RTMP, SRT, HLS, SVC), including the path from WebRTC to CDN-backed HLS for very large audiences. Own the fleet: reliability, autoscaling, placement, rollouts, observability and cost for long-lived sessions across clouds, with cost per gigabyte as a first-class metric. Gate production changes: define the validation that decides which changes, including AI-generated ones, reach live media, using behaviour tests on realistic networks, nightly telemetry scans and a public quality benchmark. Take the final escalation: handle the hardest quality, latency and production incidents, and work with enterprise customers on advanced integrations. Raise the bar: mentor senior engineers through design review, code review and hiring. About you You've owned systems where a dropped session or a bad rollout is visible to users within seconds, and you think about cost and reliability as much as features. You'd rather write the hard design doc than wait for one. A founder background is an asset here. The team is small, so you'll still write and review plenty of code. If you're looking for a large organisation with a platform team to hand problems to, or a management track, this role won't suit you. You have: Extensive backend engineering experience, including significant time owning architecture for high-scale production systems Expert proficiency in Go or an equivalent systems language (Rust, C++, Java) A track record owning real-time, stateful or latency-sensitive systems at very high scale Deep knowledge of distributed systems and networking: failure modes, placement, capacity planning and cost Strong experience with real-time media or streaming: WebRTC, SFU/MCU concepts, RTP/RTCP, DTLS, or RTMP, SRT and HLS Clear written communication: design docs and RFCs that others can act on Hands-on experience adopting AI coding and agent tools, and judgement on how to make them safe in production Bonus points: Built or operated an SFU, or contributed to Pion or another WebRTC stack Moved a stateful fleet to Kubernetes, or ran media workloads across more than one cloud Knowledge of bandwidth estimation, congestion control, simulcast, SVC and codecs (Opus, VP8/VP9, AV1) CockroachDB/PostgreSQL, RocksDB, Raft and Redis at scale Experience at developer tooling, API or SDK companies Founder or early-stage startup experience building real-time products Python or Rust alongside Go Conference talks, technical writing or notable open-source work in real-time media What makes this role exciting Scope: the infrastructure direction for video is yours to run as a product, with the authority to decide what ships. Impact: Video is Stream's most complex product, and many customers run it alongside Chat, Feeds and Moderation, so this work matters across the company. Stack: Go, Pion, WebRTC, WHIP/WHEP, RTMP, SRT, HLS, Protobuf, CockroachDB/Postgres, RocksDB, Raft and Redis, with Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT Codex in daily use. Starting point: a concrete first 90 days. Ship a validation gate on every infrastructure change that reaches production media, and move part of the fleet to Kubernetes with a cost-per-gigabyte number attached. Why join Stream? We're a Series B company with offices in Boulder, Amsterdam, Skopje and Toronto, and a team of 140+ people from 37 nationalities. We're backed by Felicis Ventures, GGV Capital, 01 Advisors, Techstars, and Arthur Ventures, with angels including Dick Costolo (ex-CEO of Twitter), Olivier Pomel (CEO of Datadog), Tom Preston-Werner (co-founder of GitHub), and Nicolas Dessaigne (co-founder of Algolia). We'll be straight with you: a startup is more demanding than a large company. There's no fixed playbook, you'll own things end to end, and you'll sometimes pick up work outside your title. That's also what makes it a fast place to grow. If you want real ownership and high scale more than structure and a set career ladder, you'll feel at home here. What we offer Company equity 28 days paid time off plus Dutch public holidays Pension plan with a company contribution NS Business Card or a company bike, covered Personal development budget of EUR 500 per year Catered lunches in the office MacBook Pro Up to EUR 60 a month toward a gym or sports club membership of your choice Highly skilled migrant (kennismigrant) visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're moving to Amsterdam This list applies to Netherlands-based employees and is adjusted to your location of residence. If you work remotely from another EU country, you'll be employed through our Employer of Record partner and get company equity plus local benefits depending on your country of employment. Our culture Stream is a casual, transparent team that aims high and supports each other. In engineering, we care about ownership and quality, and our goal is to ship stable software. Management stays hands-on, with less middle management and more time spent doing the work. If that sounds like the environment you want next, apply now. Stream is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on skills and experience, and we don't discriminate based on age, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, political opinion, disability or chronic illness, marital status, working hours, type of contract, or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an adjustment at any point in our hiring process, let us know. Hybrid office policy: applicants based (or relocating to) one of our office locations are expected to work according to the applicable local office attendance policy. Equal opportunity employer statement: Stream provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training. Note for external recruiters: We currently have this role covered and do not accept unsolicited agency resumes. We are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

As a Broker, you will build the skills, confidence and market knowledge needed to translate complex risk exposures into structured programmes and serve as a credible intermediary between clients and insurers. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organisation, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. The Global team supports multinational corporate clients across industries including manufacturing, food and agri-business, pharmaceuticals, technology, professional services, and financial institutions. You will work with colleagues in Ireland and globally. What You Will Do As a Broker you will build hands-on broking experience while supporting a portfolio of multinational clients and developing an understanding of how risk, markets, clients, and strategy come together. Analyse Risk and Build Market Insight Carry out premium and claims reporting and analysis. Develop insight into client risks across a range of industries and validate information used in insurance placements. Business and professional development in Commercial Risk, client service, communication, collaboration, problem solving, and commercial awareness. Exposure to data, analytics and technology that support risk assessment, market analysis, workflow coordination, and client-ready recommendations. Networking, mentorship, and coaching opportunities to build relationships across Aon and develop your career path. What Will Help You Succeed and Grow Skills We are looking for candidates who are curious, motivated and excited to learn. Through the Launch Programme, you will continue developing the skills and capabilities that support a successful broking and advisory career, including: Interest in business, risk, insurance, analytics, finance, economics, client service or global markets. Career interest in Risk Capital and Commercial Risk Broking. Growth Mindset - Drive to develop, welcome feedback and learn from challenges. Curiosity & Innovation - Curiosity, adaptability and willingness to question and improve ways of working. Resilience - Stay composed, optimistic and focused under pressure; know when to persist or adapt. Proactive ownership and accountability for tasks, progress and quality outcomes. Client focus - understand needs, build trust and constructively challenge thinking for lasting value. Impactful Communication - Explain complex ideas clearly, listen actively and adapt to your audience. Strategic Solutioning - Use insightful questions and structured analysis to identify client needs and effective solutions. Commerciality - Interest in market trends, client value, financial drivers and sustainable growth. Cross-Functional Collaboration - Work across teams, manage stakeholders and build networks towards shared goals. Cultivates Belonging & Support - Foster a supportive environment where colleagues feel valued, respected and able to contribute. AI & Digital Literacy - Ability and willingness to use and critically assess digital and AI tools for efficiency, insight and better decisions. Microsoft Office proficiency, including Excel, PowerPoint and Word. How We Support Our Colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. 0fc8c4e2423ec590976a.description:
Datadog Sales Engineers help qualify and close opportunities with customers and partners. You will provide technical expertise through sales presentations, product demonstrations, and supporting technical evaluations (POCs). Sales Engineers have a voice with the product team to help prioritize features based on input from customers, competitors, and partners. Additionally, you will work with various teams to resolve customer concerns, escalate bug issues, and serve as an ambassador for our brand. If you want to join a friendly, passionate team with limitless potential, we’d love to meet you!

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What You’ll Do:

  • Partner with the sales team to articulate the overall Datadog value proposition, vision and strategy to customers
  • Continually learn new technology to build competitive knowledge, technical skill, and credibility
  • Deliver product and technical presentations with potential clients
  • Have a direct line of communication with the product team to collaborate on feature requests
  • Help clients onboard the product and assist when they run into roadblocks. 
  • Think creatively about a wide variety of technical challenges during the pre-sales life cycle 

Who You Are:

  • Knowledgeable and experienced with DevOps monitoring or architecture tools. 
  • Comfortable and confident in delivering technical presentations/demos to either external customers or internal teams
  • Able to think creatively about a wide variety of challenges. You're going to find new things every day
  • Previously experienced in systems administrations: Windows or Linux
  • Able to sit up to 4 hours, traveling to and from client sites 
  • Able to travel via auto, train or air up to 25% of the time
  • Fluent in written and spoken Spanish and English

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

Benefits and Growth: 

  • Best-in-breed onboarding
  • Generous global benefits
  • Intra-departmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking
  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
  • Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing

About Us We are an AI startup founded in 2020, headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, with an AI Lab in Milan, Italy. Our expertise spans machine learning and generative AI for financial services. At Gemmo AI, we build custom AI solutions that combine automation with human insight. We use a modular approach: first we explore the highest-impact opportunities, then we design and deploy tailored solutions, and finally we help improve and maintain them over time. We believe in responsible, pragmatic AI: systems that integrate into real workflows, provide measurable value, and remain under the client's control. Our Team Forward Deployed Engineers: 25 people, including 4 Ph.D.s Leadership: 4 people We are a lean, technical-first team, and we're growing. We're looking to add 17 new Forward-Deployed AI Engineer roles before the end of the year. The Role A forward-deployed engineer works directly with the client and owns the solution end to end: from understanding the business problem, to choosing and building the right model, to shipping and running it in production. There's no handoff chain. The same engineer who hears the problem delivers the answer. In practice, the role combines three disciplines: Business analysis: understanding how a financial institution works, mapping its processes, and turning a vague request into a clear specification. ML engineering: building, evaluating and improving models, from classic prediction models to fine-tuned LLMs. Software engineering: building the APIs, integrations and applications that put models into real workflows, then deploying and maintaining them. Nobody arrives strong in all three. We hire people who are solid in at least one and eager to grow into the others. What You'll Do You'll work on AI solutions for one of the most data-rich industries in the world, in direct contact with enterprise clients. Depending on the project, you might: Sit with client stakeholders to understand a workflow and identify where AI creates measurable value Build prediction models and ML-based document analysis Fine-tune LLMs to power conversational interfaces over the client's data Extract actionable insights from large-scale datasets Design the APIs and integrations that connect your models to the client's systems Deploy, monitor and improve what you've built once it's live Both tracks involve close collaboration with senior engineers and direct exposure to enterprise clients. This is not a support role: you'll be expected to contribute from day one. What You Will Learn Running discovery with clients and translating business problems into technical plans Building and evaluating ML and generative AI solutions for financial services Designing, building and maintaining CRUD APIs to interact with users and serve models Deploying, monitoring and maintaining applications in Azure and Snowflake Communicating technical work clearly to non-technical stakeholders Who You Are You have a solid foundation in machine learning or software engineering, from your studies, research or work You enjoy understanding why something needs to be built, not just how You're comfortable talking to clients and asking questions when a problem is unclear You take ownership of outcomes, not just tasks You write clearly, because most of our communication happens in writing Interest in financial services is a plus; prior experience is not required Tech Stack We use a mix of modern tools and languages. You'll have the chance to explore and work with technologies like these: Languages: Python, SQL ML frameworks: PyTorch, XGBoost API frameworks: FastAPI Databases: Snowflake, Postgres Cloud: Azure, AWS How We Work Everyone is expected to communicate clearly, move fast, and take ownership. Communication: We run one short standup every morning to align on daily priorities. Everything else lives in writing: project documentation on Linear and GitHub, and async conversations on Slack, with dedicated channels per team and project. Rhythm and organisation: We work in weekly sprints, so priorities are always clear and nothing drags. Every Friday we run a retrospective: an open conversation about what's working and what isn't. 108e558a10a045d901a8.description: TSL - About Us TSL is a leading international technical engineering and construction partner operating across the UK, Ireland, and Mainland Europe. We focus on design and build contracts for end user clients, specialising in the Food, Pharmaceutical, Logistics, Data Centre and Advanced Manufacturing sectors. TSL is committed to creating the spaces that enable the fourth industrial revolution, whilst ensuring we leave a positive environmental and social legacy for communities across the world. Our team work with our valued clients and supply chain partners to create a simple agenda concentrated on getting things done. Above all, we are focused on delivering first class projects, executed efficiently, without compromising on safety or quality. Role purpose TSL is seeking a Project Sustainability Coordinator to support the delivery of responsible, high-performance projects across its international portfolio. You will help embed practical sustainability standards into project delivery, coordinating environmental requirements across sites while supporting TSL’s commitments to safety, quality, and schedule. Based on TSL’s Organization Context, this role contributes directly to the mission of creating facilities that enable the fourth industrial revolution while leaving a positive environmental and social legacy. You will work with project teams delivering data centre, food, and pharmaceutical facilities across EMEA, the Americas, and APAC. This role is based in our Leixlip office with local travel around Ireland and occasional international travel included. What you’ll do • Coordinate sustainability activity across multiple project sites, including national and international travel. • Support project teams with environmental management processes, documentation, and compliance requirements. • Help implement and maintain ISO 14001-aligned environmental management practices. • Assist in obtaining, collating, and managing evidence for sustainability certifications and accreditations, including BREEAM, LEED, and equivalent schemes. • Support project teams to understand certification requirements and progress targeted credits. • Draft and maintain project environmental and sustainability documentation, including Construction Environmental Management Plans, local value needs assessments, and pollution incident response plans. • Undertake construction-site inspections and work with project teams to maintain compliance with company procedures, plans, and applicable requirements. • Support preparation for client, regulator, and auditor visits. • Work with engineers, contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders to identify practical, technically sound sustainability solutions. • Communicate project sustainability requirements to supply-chain partners and promote continual improvement. • Track environmental actions, risks, evidence, and deliverables through design, construction, commissioning, and handover. • Support resource-efficiency, waste-reduction, emissions-reporting, social-value, and stakeholder-engagement initiatives. • Produce clear progress updates and reports for site-based and central teams, translating complex requirements into workable actions. What you’ll bring Essential qualifications and experience • Qualification in environmental, sustainability, ESG, engineering, or a related discipline. • Three to five years of relevant experience in sustainability, environmental coordination, construction, engineering, or another technical project environment. • Experience working in a professional environment and collaborating across multiple stakeholders. • Working knowledge of ISO 14001 and environmental management systems. • Experience working with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. • Strong written communication and report-writing capability, with confidence presenting to varied audiences when required. • Ability to handle and interpret large data sets for sustainability metrics, emissions, and construction-performance reporting. • Clear, effective verbal communication and strong interpersonal skills. • Strong logical problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn complex requirements into practical site-level actions. • A full driving licence applicable to the role’s region or country, plus willingness to travel nationally and internationally. Desirable qualifications and experience • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in an environmental or sustainability discipline. • ISO 14001 Internal Auditor qualification. • CSCS Card or regional equivalent. • Experience supporting BREEAM, LEED, or other building-rating assessments. • Experience conducting environmental or sustainability assessments and audits. • Experience planning, delivering, or calculating social value. • Construction-site experience and working knowledge of construction management, processes, activities, and terminology. • Proficiency with sustainability assessment, environmental management, or data-reporting software. • Membership, at any grade, of a relevant professional body such as IEMA or IES. • Knowledge of environmental and social global megatrends. How you’ll work This role suits someone adaptable, self-sufficient, and motivated by ownership. You will need the autonomy to progress environmental deliverables across multiple live projects, while working within clear standards, milestones, and escalation routes when decisions affect safety, quality, or delivery. TSL’s systematic, technically focused delivery model provides the structure for this role. You will apply sound judgement, maintain visibility of risks and actions, and work hands-on with project teams to make sustainability requirements achievable in real construction environments. Why join TSL You will join a team with a strong family mentality, where collaboration and mutual support matter. TSL combines an entrepreneurial, hands-on culture with rigorous safety, quality, and technical standards. This is an opportunity to influence sustainable outcomes on complex, fast-moving projects worldwide while contributing to facilities that support societal progression and long-term environmental and social value.

About Kaluza Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future. Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life. With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen. use AI-assisted development such as Claude Code to build working tools where that is the right call What you’ll bring Ideally you’ll have/be A track record of running research end to end that other teams used in product or roadmap decisions, with strong data literacy: you combine qualitative methods with behavioural data and know what the numbers can and can’t tell us Experience researching in B2B or B2B2C or enterprise contexts, including technical users such as developers (eg SDKs, APIs or documentation), or a strong appetite to learn how Experience coaching non-researchers in research fundamentals (interviewing, bias mitigation, ethical handling of user data) so they can self-serve Experience on a platform or multi-client product, spotting patterns across customers, and familiarity with journey mapping or service design methods Experience in research operations or enablement, such as participant recruitment, consent and data governance, repositories or tool selection, with judgement on when to build and when to buy Confidence working with some autonomy across a distributed, international team What will set you apart You’ve built a tool, repository or pipeline that measurably cut the time from research signal to team-wide insight You’ve found a way to measure developer experience where there was no playbook (eg time to first successful call, or where developers drop off) You’ve made the case for research with real numbers, and followed your research after the readout to see what happened Where you'll work We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives. 1112e3b288d4aefad96e.description: Position Description Enterprise Services IT Delivery is seeking a Software Asset Management Specialist to join the Software Asset Management team. The Software Asset Management team is responsible for the governance, optimisation, compliance and commercial management of software assets across ESB. This role provides an opportunity to develop and apply expertise in software licensing, vendor management, software renewals, licence optimisation, compliance assurance and software governance. Working as part of a highly collaborative team, you will engage with business users, technical teams and software vendors to ensure software assets are managed effectively, licensing obligations are met, and software investments deliver maximum value to ESB. In support of ESB's strategic objectives of decarbonising electricity, building resilient infrastructure and empowering customers, you will help ensure ESB's software estate is managed efficiently, securely and compliantly while supporting cost optimisation and technology enablement across the organisation. Key Responsibilities Administer and govern software licensing processes including software requests, software assignments and licence entitlement management. Maintain current list of application owners across the enterprise in support of the IT Store function. Support software compliance activities and maintain accurate software asset and entitlement records. Lead software usage reviews, licence optimisation initiatives and software re-harvesting activities to maximise business value and minimise unnecessary spend. Support software renewal activities through engagement with technical approvers, procurement and business stakeholders. Provide advice and support to users and stakeholders on software licensing policies, governance requirements and approved software solutions. Develop and maintain software asset management processes, procedures, reports and documentation to support governance and continuous improvement. Experience and Qualifications Essential Third-level qualification in Information Technology, Business Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience. A minimum of 3 years’ experience in software licensing, software asset management, IT asset management or a comparable technology governance or operational role. Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to review software usage, licensing information and commercial data. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience engaging professionally with stakeholders and suppliers. Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across teams and manage competing priorities in a structured and effective manner. Desirable Knowledge of Software Asset Management (SAM) principles and best practice. Experience with software asset management or software inventory tools. Knowledge of Microsoft and enterprise software licensing programmes. Experience supporting software procurement, renewals, compliance reviews or optimisation initiatives. Familiarisation with Power BI concepts and dashboard creation. Location This position will be based in ESB’s Head Office at Fitzwilliam 27, Dublin 2. Smart Working at ESB is designed to make ‘in-person’ time together as purposeful as possible while also enabling the effective use of digital tools and hybrid arrangements to preserve our commitment to flexibility. The successful candidate may work flexibly within the jurisdiction where they have been employed, with attendance at the workplace for in-person collaboration at least two days per week. All Smart Working arrangements are subject to regular review based on the operational requirements of the role, the team, and the business. Reporting To Software Asset Management Team Lead, IT Delivery. Why Work with Us? Opportunity to lead Ireland’s transition to net zero carbon future Career development through mentoring and training Corporate Social Responsibility Opportunities Sports and Social Clubs Networking opportunities Credit Union Generous Pension Access to staff well-being programmes Generous parental leave entitlements Strong values-based and inclusive culture Strong commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion Great team environment working to our Core Values: Courageous, Caring, Driven and Trusted Salary €49,500 - €58,500 per annum (depending on experience) Closing Date 26th October 2026 Interview Candidates who are shortlisted for interview will complete a Behavioural Interview based on each of the following Behaviours, which underpin how we work at ESB and are critical to delivering our strategy: Accountable and Ethical Collaborative Growing and Adaptive Proactive Respectful and Supportive More information available on Our People Promise Notes Your application will be held in reserve for 6 months should you be suitable for the role. The successful candidate will be required to evidence their right to work in the Republic of Ireland prior to commencement of employment.
