About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Technical Recruiter at Anthropic, you will be instrumental in shaping the future of our organization by identifying, engaging, and hiring the best and brightest minds across a range of disciplines. As we continue to push the boundaries of AI research and development, we need a passionate recruiter who can help us build a world-class team dedicated to creating safe and beneficial AI systems.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute strategic recruiting plans to identify and source highly qualified candidates
  • Partner with technical and non-technical hiring managers and interviewers to understand hiring needs, team matching, required skills and qualifications
  • Implement recruiting processes and programs such as developing targeted outreach campaigns, building connections with industry leaders, and removing any unfair biases from the hiring process 
  • Collaborate with leadership and cross-functional partners to understand organizational needs and map out long-term talent acquisition strategies that balance priorities across all technical teams
  • Enhance Anthropic’s employer brand to showcase our mission, culture, and values to candidates
  • Provide an exceptional candidate experience throughout the recruiting process

Minimum qualifications

  • Deep full lifecycle recruiting experience, with substantial time supporting technical engineering organizations
  • Proficiency with an applicant tracking system like Greenhouse and other modern sourcing tools
  • Experience partnering directly with hiring managers on intake, bar calibration, and interview loop design
  • Sound independent judgment on candidate quality, and the ability to independently partner with multiple hiring managers are complex searches
  • Genuine interest in Anthropic's mission and in the role a strong security function plays in achieving it

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience recruiting at a high-growth technology, AI, or machine learning company
  • Working knowledge of the security credential landscape and clear judgment about where those credentials carry signal and where they do not
  • Experience hiring for engineering, incident response, threat intelligence, insider risk, or physical security
  • Experience improving recruiting processes, market maps, or interview architecture where they were thin or absent
  • Comfort using LLMs to accelerate sourcing, research, and market mapping

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$240,000—$295,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. We need someone who has shipped hardware at scale, has a realistic view of ODM/CM schedules and where they break, and is comfortable owning consequential program calls without a large organization behind them. 

Key responsibilities

  • Own the integrated hardware systems program plan across board, chassis, rack, and interconnect — from requirements through EVT/DVT/PVT, qualification, and production ramp — and be the source of truth on schedule, risk, and readiness.
  • Drive execution with ODMs, contract manufacturers, and component/optics vendors: SOWs, build schedules, deliverable tracking, factory readiness, and escalation when they slip.
  • Stand up and run the NPI cadence — build matrix, engineering reviews, DFx, issue triage, exit criteria — and keep it lightweight enough that a small, senior team actually uses it.
  • Drive the bring-up and validation program for new platforms: lab and pilot-rack logistics, firmware/BMC/diagnostics coordination, test coverage, and the reliability and telemetry targets a platform has to hit before it enters the fleet.
  • Own the interfaces that make or break a hardware program: silicon (samples, package, power/thermal envelopes), datacenter (power, cooling, rack integration, deployment windows), infrastructure software (management plane, provisioning, telemetry), and supply chain (long-lead components, second-sourcing, allocation).
  • Run partner and technology evaluations as a program — candidate ODMs, reference platforms, connector/optics/memory options — and land build / buy / co-design recommendations with the architecture team.
  • Own program communication upward and outward — for an audience that ranges from architects to executives.
  • Develop and share AI-assisted approaches to hardware program management — issue-tracker synthesis, build-readiness checking, spec/BOM consistency, ODM-report digestion.

Minimum qualifications

  • 8+ years in hardware systems / NPI program management for compute, networking, storage, or accelerator platforms.
  • Direct ownership of at least one platform from concept through volume production — you can walk through its EVT/DVT/PVT arc, what broke, and how you recovered.
  • Working technical fluency across the hardware stack — power delivery, thermal, mechanical, high-speed interconnect, board design, system management — sufficient to interrogate status and push back credibly on architects and vendors.
  • Experience managing ODMs/CMs and component vendors, including SOW negotiation, build tracking, quality escapes, and escalation.
  • Track record of standing up program mechanisms on a new or early-stage hardware effort, not just operating inside a mature PLC.
  • Strong written communication — plans, reviews, and exec updates that many teams depend on.
  • Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited process in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with AI/ML accelerator systems (GPU, TPU, custom ASIC), HPC, or hyperscale datacenter platforms and their scale-up / scale-out fabrics.
  • Experience taking a first-generation, custom-silicon-based system from bring-up through fleet deployment.
  • Experience with liquid-cooled and/or high-density rack architectures, rack level high power distribution, or optical interconnect programs.
  • Familiarity with the chip-package-system interface and coordinating tightly with a silicon team.
  • Experience with datacenter integration, deployment, and fleet-scale reliability/RAS programs.
  • Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.
  • BS/MS in EE, CE, ME, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

About the Interpretability team

When you see what modern language models are capable of, do you wonder, "How do these things work? How can we trust them?"

The Interpretability team’s mission is to reverse engineer how trained models work, and Interpretability research is one of Anthropic’s core research bets on AI safety. We believe that a mechanistic understanding is the most robust way to make advanced systems safe. 

People mean many different things by "interpretability". We're focused on mechanistic interpretability, which aims to discover how neural network parameters map to meaningful algorithms. Some useful analogies might be to think of us as trying to do "biology" or "neuroscience" of neural networks, or as treating neural networks as binary computer programs we're trying to "reverse engineer".

We aim to create a solid scientific foundation for mechanistically understanding neural networks and making them safe (see our vision post). We have focused on resolving the issue of "superposition" (see Toy Models of Superposition, Superposition, Memorization, and Double Descent, and our May 2023 update), which causes the computational units of the models, like neurons and attention heads, to be individually uninterpretable, and on finding ways to decompose models into more interpretable components. Our subsequent work which found millions of features in Claude 3.0 Sonnet, one of our production language models, represents progress in this direction. In our most recent work, we developed methods that allow us to build circuits using features and use these circuits to understand the mechanisms associated with a model's computation and study specific examples of multi-hop reasoning, planning, and chain-of-thought faithfulness on Claude Haiku 3.5, one of our production models.” This is a stepping stone towards our overall goal of mechanistically understanding neural networks.

A few places to learn more about our work and team are this introduction to Interpretability from our research lead, Chris Olah, Stanford CS25 lecture given by Josh Batson, and TWIML AI podcast with Emmanuel Ameisen.

Some of our team's notable publications include and our Circuits’ Methods and Biology papers, Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet, Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning, A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits, In-context Learning and Induction Heads, and Toy Models of Superposition. This work builds on ideas from members' work prior to Anthropic such as the original circuits thread, Multimodal Neurons, Activation Atlases, and Building Blocks.

As a manager on the Interpretability team, you'll support a team of expert researchers and engineers who are trying to understand at a deep, mechanistic level, how modern large language models work internally. 

Few things can accelerate this work more than great managers. Your work as manager will be critical in making sure that our fast-growing team is able to meet its ambitious safety research goals over the coming years. In this role, you will partner closely with an individual contributor research lead to drive the team's success, translating cutting-edge research ideas into tangible goals and overseeing their execution. You will manage team execution, careers and performance, facilitate relationships within and across teams, and drive the hiring pipeline. 

If you're more interested in making individual direct technical contributions to our research as the primary focus of your role, feel free to apply to our Research Scientist or Research Engineer roles instead.

  • Partner with a research lead on direction, project planning and execution, hiring, and people development

  • Coach and support team members to have more impact and develop in their careers

  • Help identify and support opportunities for collaboration with other teams across Anthropic

  • Maintain a deep understanding of the team's technical work and its implications for AI safety

  • Are an experienced manager (minimum 2-5 years) with a track record of effectively leading highly technical research and/or engineering teams 
  • Have a background in machine learning, AI, or a related technical field
  • Actively enjoy people management and are experienced with coaching and mentorship, performance evaluation, career development, and hiring for technical roles
  • Have strong project management skills, including prioritization and cross-functional coordination and collaboration
  • Have managed technical teams through periods of ambiguity and change
  • Are a quick learner, capable of understanding and contributing to discussions on complex technical topics and are motivated to learn about our research
  • Are a strong communicator both in speaking and in writing
  • Believe that advanced AI systems could have a transformative effect on the world, and are passionate about helping make sure that transformation goes well

Strong candidates may also have

  • Experience scaling engineering infrastructure
  • Experience working on open-ended, exploratory research agendas aimed at foundational insights
  • Some familiarity with our work and mechanistic interpretability

  • Write the specifications and interface definitions that others design against and keep them coherent as the architecture converges
  • Make and own directional calls: technology and IP selection, where we build versus buy versus license, and where we take design authority versus rely on partners
  • Build and share AI-assisted approaches to the code-like parts of your domain, and help the team learn what Claude can genuinely accelerate
  • Contribute to the architecture and micro-architecture discussion from your domain's perspective, including the tradeoffs your area imposes on the rest of the chip
  • Partner with Anthropic's inference, performance, kernels, and infrastructure teams on hardware-software co-design, and with our hardware systems team on bring-up and integration
  • Support first-silicon bring-up and debug when it arrives, regardless of which domain you came in through

Minimum qualifications

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one silicon domain: front-end design, pre-silicon verification, physical design, design for test, analog and mixed-signal, technology and foundry, design infrastructure, or packaging and signal/power integrity
  • Direct personal contribution to silicon that taped out and shipped, with ownership you can speak to in detail
  • Working fluency in the domains adjacent to your own, sufficient to reason about chip-level tradeoffs outside your specialty
  • Experience working with external partners — ASIC houses, IP vendors, foundries, or test partners — including reviewing their work and holding a technical bar
  • Track record of owning directional technical decisions and their consequences, not only making recommendations
  • Practical experience using AI coding tools in your own work, and clear ideas about where they help and where they do not
  • Clear written and verbal communication, and experience driving alignment across teams and organizations
  • Comfort operating with high autonomy and little scaffolding on a highly dynamic program

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience on machine learning accelerators, high-performance compute, or other large, high-bandwidth designs
  • Experience on a founding or early-stage silicon team, including standing up flows, methodology, or tooling from nothing
  • Experience with both partner-executed and fully in-house programs, and a view on the tradeoffs between them
  • Familiarity with the chip-package-system interface and the tradeoffs that cross it
  • Experience with hardware-software co-design and working directly with compiler, kernel, or runtime teams
  • Experience building or extending AI-assisted design, verification, or physical design flows
  • Depth in memory subsystems, on-die interconnect, numerics, or low-power design

Representative projects

  • Writing the specification for a compute datapath and defending its numeric format strategy against the alternatives
  • Standing up front-end flows and release management from scratch, then handing releases to an ASIC partner on a fixed cadence
  • Running fast in-house place-and-route loops on a critical block and feeding PPA reality back into the architecture
  • Selecting and qualifying PHY IP, then validating it on first silicon
  • Building a formal verification methodology for a new block and deciding where formal earns its keep versus simulation
  • Defining test strategy and the automated-test-equipment handoff interface with our partner
  • Prototyping a Claude-assisted workflow for RTL review, coverage triage, or specification consistency checking, and reporting honestly on what it did and did not do
  • Debugging a first-silicon failure that crosses your domain and someone else's

6746192fa6d509aa1b99.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Scientists use Claude across the life sciences, from drug discovery and research biology to clinical development and manufacturing. To support that work, Anthropic introduced the Life Sciences Verification Program (LSVP), which gives verified life science professionals access to Claude with a refined set of safeguards that is more permissive for biology-related work. The program is in beta.We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own the program of work that expands that access and helps scale it with safety in mind.

Each expansion depends on many teams at once and no single team owns the path end to end. You'll become the single owner of that program, the person who knows what each expansion requires, where every workstream stands, what it is waiting on, and who needs to decide. This is a cross-org execution role, not a research role, and it does not require a life sciences background. LSVP is the starting point, and the scope will grow alongside Anthropic's broader work in the life sciences. Over time, more of the life sciences community can get verified access, and each new expansion takes less bespoke effort than the last.

Responsibilities

  • Own the program for expanding access to Anthropic's life sciences verification programs: scoping, sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs across safeguards, platform, and product engineering teams
  • Scope and drive the cross-org engineering work that each expansion requires, from new plan and account types to new platforms
  • Partner with the product manager to turn program goals into a sequenced plan with clear owners and dates
  • Drive clarity on data access, retention, and review requirements, and on the changes they require across safeguards, access, and provisioning
  • Drive user experience scoping across the Claude product surfaces where the program is available
  • Find and remove the technical blockers that keep eligible organizations from accessing life sciences capabilities
  • Establish the operating rhythm: a single view of workstreams, owners, dependencies, risks, and status, with planning, escalation paths, and launch coordination across orgs
  • Convert recurring efforts into documented, repeatable processes so that each new expansion requires less bespoke coordination

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have several years of experience in technical program management, with a track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs
  • Have experience coordinating across multiple engineering teams and organizations simultaneously, including safeguards, platform, and product partners
  • Can engage meaningfully with the engineers doing the work, from platform and access systems to product surfaces
  • Are highly organized and can manage multiple parallel workstreams effectively across distributed teams
  • Thrive in unstructured environments with a knack for bringing order to chaos and creating clarity in ambiguous situations
  • Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority
  • Have worked on cloud or platform programs (preferred but not required)
  • Do not need a life sciences background. This is not a research role, and no life sciences experience is required
  • Are passionate about Anthropic's mission and interested in the challenges of bringing AI capabilities to the life sciences community safely and reliably

 

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$290,000—$365,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

681bc03462474e4318f6.description: TL;DR:  As our first Executive Assistant, you'll support Conduct's founders by protecting their time, keeping priorities moving and making the company feel sharper in how it runs day to day. It's a high-trust role, close to every big decision, at a company running faster than ever.   WHY CONDUCT   We believe the world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the decade-old systems they run on. Today they don't.  Every process change, every new product line runs into software systems layered with decades of custom code and complexity no human mind can fully comprehend. New requirements take months to ship, system migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain.  We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed and ambition. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems, we've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service.  We're a small, talent-dense team doing our life's work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world's largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out.   WHAT YOU'LL OWN   You'll work side by side with our three founders as they tackle one of the most complex problems of our generation. Their time is one of the most valuable things we have, and you'll help to decide how it gets spent. One day that means getting a CEO to a customer in Germany. The next, it's prepping a board meeting or landing a candidate we've been chasing for months. Plans often change hourly and you'll help keep everything on track. You'll be our first EA, so you'll set the standard for how we support the founders. As we grow, the team around you might too, and you'll help shape how it works. Few roles give you this view of how a generational company gets built, and as we scale, your scope grows with us.  In practice:    Help run packed founder calendars and decide what they spend their time on    Set up the meetings that move Conduct forward, with enterprise customers, investors and partners, and make sure everyone walks in prepared and walks out with next steps    Plan global founder travel and fix it fast when things don’t go to plan    Live in founder inboxes and threads, prioritising by what matters most to the business, handling what you can and flagging what you can’t    Write on the founders' behalf to customers, investors and partners, and get every detail right    Keep board and investor meetings running smoothly, from scheduling to follow-ups    Help candidates have a great first experience of Conduct    Spot what's slowing the team down and build the fix     WHO WE HIRE   You're the person everyone goes to when something needs to get done properly. You're sharp, calm under pressure and good with people, and you'd rather be in the room where decisions happen than watching from the outside. You might already be an EA, or you might be in a role where you've quietly been doing the job of one.  In practice that tends to look like:    You've supported founders, CEOs, or senior execs in a high-pressure, high-excellence environment, ideally a fast-scaling startup, and you know how to keep up    You thrive when things are messy and moving fast, and you bring structure without waiting to be asked    You're smart and proactive, and you see what's needed before anyone asks    You're happy to push back, even with a founder, when something doesn't need to happen    You communicate clearly and confidently, in writing and in person, whether it's an investor, a customer or a new hire    You bring maturity and sound judgement to confidential matters    When something doesn't work, you fix it or automate it, and you'll happily pick up work that's nowhere near your job description    You have a zero-error mindset: anything with your name or a founder's on it is right first time, even on the busiest days    Speaking German is a plus    Find  Jobs in United Kingdom  on Arbeitnow

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team accelerates the work of organizations doing some of the world's most important under-resourced work: nonprofits, education institutions, scientific researchers, and organizations advancing economic mobility. Research institutions sit at the center of that mission. They produce the science the rest of the world builds on, and they are structurally short on time, budget, and technical capacity to figure out new technology on their own.

You will lead our targeted approach to research institutes and research intensive universities globally. Where our scaled motion reaches thousands of organizations one to many, this role is the opposite end of the same ecosystem: a deliberately short list of institutions where depth matters, where a lab, a department, or a whole campus adopting Claude changes what science gets done, and where the buying process runs through provosts, research offices, procurement, grant budgets, and security review.

Reach comes first, and commercial results follow from it. That ordering is deliberate and it is shared across every leader on this team: a research institute that adopts Claude to move its science faster is a win on its own terms, and you will be measured on creating that value with the institutions that matter most, not only on pipeline. You are the single accountable owner for the research Enterprise book globally: its target list, its AEs, its numbers, and its field voice inside Anthropic.

You are half seller, half domain translator. You will personally run the most complex institutional deals, and you will be credible in a room of scientists and research leaders. You know how research is funded, how a university decides, and what it takes for a research sales motion to land in a software company. You will bring that knowledge to the product, applied AI, and marketing teams who build for this audience.

This is a player coach seat. You will be directly involved in deals and directing the account executives who cover research institutes and universities today, and the role is expected to grow thoughtfully with more AEs in key regions globally.

Key responsibilities

  • Co-design our global research strategy: the target list of research institutes and research intensive universities that advance scientific discovery. 
  • Serve as the lead on our most complex institutional deals — setting the pursuit strategy, opening doors with lab and research-office leadership, university provosts, and personally resolving the toughest hurdles: procurement, security review, and grant-funded budgets.
  • Direct and coach the account executives working research accounts today: joint account plans, deal reviews, and a repeatable motion for landing a university and expanding within it.
  • Build the institutional playbook: how an institute goes from a pilot to a working deployment across a department, what good adoption looks like, and when to bring in applied AI, customer success, or partners.
  • Own the book's numbers, institutions reached, activated, and expanded against goals, and use them to decide where the effort goes next.
  • Work in lockstep with our PLG 1:many motion, so that an institution moves cleanly between scaled programs and direct coverage in both directions.

Minimum qualifications

  • Research sales. You have sold software as a service into universities, research institutes, or academic medical centers, and you have personally closed complex institutional agreements involving procurement, security review, and multiple decision makers.
  • Science background. You have trained or worked in a scientific field, or spent a meaningful part of your career selling to or building for scientists, and you can hold a credible conversation with a principal investigator about their research. 
  • Sales leadership. You have led a sales business end to end and been the accountable owner for its results, whether as a team lead, a player coach, or the sole owner of a strategic book.

Preferred qualifications

  • Global research landscape: experience selling to universities or research institutes in more than one region, an understanding of how funding and procurement differ from country to country, and comfort working across time zones with regional teams. 
  • Experience with research funding: grants, indirect costs, and how a fixed annual budget shapes what an institution can buy.
  • Track record landing an institution wide agreement at a research intensive university, and expanding from a single department to a campus or system.
  • Familiarity with how AI is already used in research settings, and a point of view on where it should go next.
  • Experience working with academic consortia, national labs, or research networks.
  • An impact, education, research, or mission driven go to market background, and genuine interest in these institutions' constraints.
  • A daily working habit with Claude, and agentic workflows you have built for yourself.

You might thrive here if you

  • Want your work measured in science that moves faster, not only in pipeline.
  • Have sat in a faculty meeting or a research office and know why the obvious commercial playbook does not work there.
  • Are comfortable being the only person accountable for a book while depending on teams you do not manage.
  • Would rather close the first three institutional deals yourself and write the playbook from what you learned than write the strategy deck first.
  • Find the constraint interesting rather than frustrating: long procurement cycles, grant timelines, and security reviews are the job, not an obstacle to it.

Work on classification, retrieval, ranking, personalization and evaluation, taking ownership from model development to production deployment. This role is for engineers who enjoy solving practical ML problems, improving model quality and shipping reliable systems used by real users. Focus Build and improve ML models for classification, ranking, retrieval and personalization. Develop efficient classifiers and optimize model accuracy, precision, latency and cost. Improve search relevance and context retrieval using embeddings, hybrid search and reranking. Build personalization models that learn from user behavior while respecting privacy. Develop evaluation pipelines, labeled datasets and metrics to measure model quality. Fine-tune and adapt existing models when supported by sufficient data. Hands-on experience building and deploying ML models in production. Experience in classification, ranking, retrieval, recommendation systems or personalization. Able to balance model quality, latency, cost and reliability. Strong ownership, problem-solving skills Outcomes ML models in production meet expected accuracy, relevance, latency and reliability targets. Classification and ranking improvements deliver measurable gains in model quality. Evaluation pipelines identify regressions and support reliable model releases. Training, inference and data pipelines are robust, reproducible and maintainable. Model improvements are driven by real-world feedback and measurable results. Collaborates effectively with engineering and product teams to deliver reliable ML-powered features. How We Work The best products in the world are built by small, world-class teams. We are a high-talent-density, hands-on team. We make decisions collectively and move quickly, balancing high-quality work with continuous learning. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us.

6b86418e1d50c81ec23d.description: Who We Are At CarGurus (NASDAQ: CARG), our mission is to give people the power to reach their destination. We started as a small team of developers determined to bring trust and transparency to car shopping. Since then, our history of innovation and go-to-market acceleration has driven industry-leading growth. In fact, we’re the largest and fastest-growing automotive marketplace, and we’ve been profitable for over 15 years. What We Do The market is evolving, and we are too, moving the entire automotive journey online and guiding our customers through every step. That includes everything from the sale of an old car to the financing, purchase, and delivery of a new one. Today, tens of millions of consumers visit CarGurus.com each month, and ~30,000 dealerships use our products. But they're not the only ones who love CarGurus—our employees do, too. We have a people-first culture that fosters kindness, collaboration, and innovation, and empowers our Gurus with tools to fuel their career growth. Disrupting a trillion-dollar industry requires fresh and diverse perspectives. Come join us for the ride! Role Overview The Associate Systems Administrator is an entry-level position within the IT Systems team based in our Dublin office. This role serves as a critical bridge between our IT Service Desk and Global Systems functions, primarily focusing on supporting our EU and UK-based employees. You will work closely with the IT Service Desk team to resolve technical escalations while aligning with US-based systems engineers to maintain global applications, security policies, patching standards, and network infrastructure across our European locations. This role requires a blend of operational support, technical curiosity, and a commitment to maintaining a secure, highly available environment. On Call work may be required with this roll as needed by the business. In addition to the responsibilities above, this role also requires regular physical activity, including moving around the office to assist with IT or AV event related tasks, lifting and carrying equipment (upwards of 50lbs), moving tables and chairs, and plugging in devices under desks and other confined spaces. The Associate Systems Administrator must be able to perform these duties safely and efficiently as part of their responsibilities. What You'll Do System Administration & Support Perform daily monitoring, management, and troubleshooting for core corporate enterprise software platforms. Assist with the configuration, deployment, and maintenance of identity platforms and collaboration tools. Follow established change management procedures for system updates and modifications. Maintain accurate system documentation, including runbooks and knowledge base articles for the Service Desk. Workspace & Endpoint Management Support the administration of Mobile Device Management (MDM) solutions such as Jamf and Microsoft Intune. Assist in managing end-user devices, including software deployments, VDI deployment and desktop configurations. Help implement and enforce security measures like software patches and OS updates. Networking & Infrastructure Provide first-level support for network escalations, including Wi-Fi, VPN, and firewall issues. Assist with basic network troubleshooting and performance monitoring for EU office environments. Support the setup and maintenance of local network hardware under senior guidance. Identity & Security Compliance Manage user lifecycles within identity platforms (e.g., Okta) to ensure appropriate access controls. Contribute to incident response efforts by participating in a regional on-call rotation. Review incoming IT requests to ensure alignment with company Information Security and governance policies. What You'll Bring Required Skills & Experience Foundational experience with Identity and Access Management (IAM) platforms such as Okta or OneLogin. Proficiency working within enterprise ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow, Atlassian/Jira). Experience with enterprise collaboration tools including Google Workspace, Microsoft O365, and Slack. Exposure to MDM tools such as Microsoft Intune or Jamf. Basic understanding of enterprise networking principles and troubleshooting techniques.Demonstrated ability to document technical processes and follow standard operating procedures. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Audiovisual (AV) setup and troubleshooting for conference rooms. Basic administration experience with enterprise cloud-based telephony systems (e.g., Dialpad). A background in Systems Administration (min 2 years experience) and some experience with IT support or service desk operations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across time zones. The displayed range represents the expected annual base salary / On-Target Earnings (OTE) for this position. On-Target Earnings (OTE) is inclusive of base salary and on-target commission earnings, which applies exclusively to sales roles. Individual pay within this range is determined by work location and other factors such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. This annual base salary forms part of a comprehensive Total Rewards Package. In addition to benefits, this role may qualify for discretionary bonuses/incentives and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). Position Pay Range €38.000—€48.000 EUR Working at CarGurus We reward our Gurus’ curiosity and passion with best-in-class benefits and compensation, including equity for all employees, both when they start and as they continue to grow with us. Our career development and corporate giving programs, as well as our employee resource groups (ERGs) and communities, help people build connections while making an impact in personally meaningful ways. A flexible hybrid model and robust time off policies encourage work-life balance and individual well-being. Thoughtful perks like daily free lunch, a new car discount, meditation and fitness apps, commuting cost coverage, and more help our people create space for what matters most in their personal and professional lives. CarGurus may require in-person interviews as part of our hiring process, particularly for positions based in our Boston and Dublin offices. Candidates selected for an in-person interview will be notified in advance. Please be aware that travel expenses are the responsibility of the candidate. We welcome all CarGurus strives to be a place to which people can bring the ultimate expression of themselves and their potential—starting with our hiring process. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, or sexual orientation. We foster an inclusive environment that values people for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. That’s why we hope you’ll apply even if you don’t check every box listed in the job description. We also encourage you to tell your recruiter if you require accommodations to participate in our hiring process due to a disability so we can provide the appropriate support. We want to know what only you can bring to CarGurus.

6ba9247cc0c5495d33d9.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a GTM Recruiter you'll help GitLab build the go-to-market teams that drive our growth. In this individual contributor role, you'll partner with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Professional Services, Field Operations, Enablement and Ecosystems and own searches from intake through close. You'll build inclusive pipelines and use data and market insight to guide hiring decisions, while growing into a trusted talent advisor.

What you'll do

  • Manage full-cycle searches for Account Executives, Solutions Architects, Customer Success, Sales Development, and Sales Operations, delivering against agreed recruiting goals and key metrics with accurate, timely documentation in Greenhouse.
  • Lead intake and kickoff conversations to align hiring teams on role scope, territory or segment, quota and ramp expectations, interview plans, and timelines, with senior team guidance as needed.
  • Partner with hiring teams on structured, equitable interviews with clear competencies and actionable feedback; challenge assumptions and escalate risks or blockers early.
  • Use talent-market research, compensation and on-target earnings (OTE) benchmarks, funnel metrics, and candidate feedback to shape search strategy and address hiring issues.
  • Assess sales candidates on track record, quota attainment, deal complexity, and experience relevant to GitLab's sales segments and approach.
  • Build research-based, diversity-focused sourcing plans that balance applicants, passive talent, referrals, internal talent, and targeted outreach.
  • Deliver a thoughtful candidate experience through disciplined pipeline management, proactive communication, timely feedback, and offer negotiations that clearly explain compensation and OTE.
  • Improve recruiting practices by sharing learnings and reusable resources, using artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly, and representing GitLab's mission, values, and culture.

What you'll bring

  • Intermediate-level recruiting experience, with a track record of owning full-cycle searches independently.
  • Sales or go-to-market recruiting experience, or a strong interest in learning sales segments, quotas, OTE, ramp time, territory design, and sales cycles.
  • Developing advisor skills: building stakeholder trust, influencing without authority, and managing hiring team expectations.
  • Experience building proactive, diversity-focused sourcing strategies and balanced pipelines.
  • A data-informed approach that turns funnel insights into practical actions.
  • Strong organization across multiple requisitions and clear written and verbal communication across time zones, with attention to detail and candidate care.
  • Experience with an applicant tracking system and recruiting tools such as Greenhouse, Metaview, LinkedIn Recruiter, LinkedIn Insights, SeekOut, or comparable platforms; ability to evaluate AI-generated work, protect confidential information, and share responsible workflows with team members.
  • Technology or business-to-business (B2B) software recruiting experience is helpful, not required.

About the team

We work in a globally distributed, remote-first Talent Acquisition team where clear communication and reliable follow-through matter. Guided by GitLab’s operating principles, including Speed with Quality, Ownership Mindset, and Customer Outcomes, we take ownership, move with urgency and rigor, and focus on hiring outcomes that matter to our internal customers. We share learnings and create reusable resources to continually improve the quality and consistency of hiring across GTM teams.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

United States Salary Range
$86,400—$146,400 USD

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave

Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. 6c0a84646adf2223c886.description: Ryanair, over our 40 year history has grown to become Europe's largest airline group connecting more guests across more routes than any other European carrier. We are a fast-paced, ambitious and innovative company, offering exciting career opportunities across aviation, technology, operations and support functions. Now is a fantastic time to join as we look to grow to over 800 aircraft and 300m guests within the next 8 years. Ryanair is currently hiring for a Supply Chain Analyst to join Europe's Largest Airline Group. This is a great time to join Ryanair, as we look to grow toward 300M Passengers and 800 Aircraft by 2034. The Supply Chain Analyst will be responsible for supporting the Supply Chain Analytics Manager in analysing supply chain, procurement and materials data within the Engineering Materials department. The role will assist in identifying opportunities to improve processes, reporting, data accuracy and operational efficiency, with a specific focus on procurement activity, supplier performance, purchase order management and material availability. This individual will support the development of dashboards, KPIs and reporting tools to improve visibility across the Materials department and help ensure that purchasing and supply chain decisions are data-driven. The role will involve working closely with internal stakeholders to support the airline’s operational requirements. This role is designed for a candidate beginning their career in supply chain, procurement, data analytics or aviation materials management. Key Responsibilities Support the Supply Chain Analytics Manager in reviewing and improving processes across the Engineering Materials department Assist in analysing procurement activity, including purchase order creation, open order management, supplier follow-up, overdue orders, delivery performance and order closure. Support the mapping and documentation of procurement processes to identify inefficiencies, duplication, manual work and opportunities for improvement and cost savings. Assist in the development of standardised procurement reports, dashboards and tracking tools to improve visibility of purchasing activity. Analyse procurement and supplier data to identify trends, recurring issues, delays and opportunities to improve material availability. Support the tracking of open purchase orders, overdue orders, supplier acknowledgements, expected delivery dates and lead time performance. Assist in identifying purchasing bottlenecks and support the implementation of practical process improvements. Support the development and maintenance of KPIs for procurement, inventory, supplier performance and wider supply chain activity. Gather, clean and validate data from procurement, inventory and materials systems to support accurate reporting and analysis. Support demand and usage reviews, including seasonal analysis, line maintenance requirements and heavy maintenance requirements. Work with the LABs / BI teams to support the development of internal reporting tools and dashboards. Assist in improving data quality within procurement and materials systems by identifying inconsistencies, missing information and reporting gaps. Support continuous improvement projects across the Materials department. Collaborate with Procurement, Planning, Stores, Logistics, Repairs, Finance and Engineering teams to gather information and support process improvement initiatives. Assist in preparing presentations, reports and analysis for internal meetings and management reviews. Provide general analytical and administrative support to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager as required. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or relevant third-level qualification in Supply Chain Management, Business, Data Analytics, Logistics, Procurement, Engineering, Aviation Management or a related field preferred. Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving ability. Good working knowledge of Microsoft Exposure to Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python or other data analytics tools would be an advantage. Understanding of basic supply chain, procurement or inventory concepts would be beneficial. No prior aviation experience required, but an interest in aviation, engineering materials or aircraft spare parts would be advantageous. Skills Strong analytical and numerical skills. High attention to detail and accuracy. Good Microsoft capability. Ability to gather, clean, organise and interpret data. Good written and verbal communication skills. Strong organisational skills and ability to manage assigned tasks. Ability to work as part of a team in a fast-paced operational environment. Problem-solving mindset and proactive approach. Ability to identify process gaps and suggest improvements. Strong follow-through and ownership of assigned work. Ability to work with multiple internal stakeholders. Competitive salary Discounted and unlimited travel to over 250 destinations Defined Contribution Pension Scheme Death in Service Benefit – Up to 2 times of annual basic salary 20 Days Annual Leave – Increasing to 22 days after 12 months and 25 days after 3 years of continuous service. Option for up to 5 additional unpaid leave days per year Cycle 2 Work Scheme Unrivalled career progression

6c2681390ad3d67f5797.description: To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts. About Futureforce University Recruiting Our Futureforce University Recruiting program is dedicated to attracting, retaining and cultivating talent. Our interns and new graduates work on real projects that affect how our business runs, giving them the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the future of our company. With offices all over the world, our recruits have the chance to collaborate and connect with fellow employees on a global scale. We offer job shadowing, mentorship programs, talent development courses, and much more. Job Category Sales Job Details About Salesforce Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce. Fixed-term contract Duration: 12 months Start Date: February 2027 We are thrilled to invite ambitious graduate candidates who would like to build a career in Salesforce to apply for the next cohort of our EMEA Graduate Rotation Program - Solution Engineering Path . This exciting 12-month program is designed to give graduates exposure to both solution engineering and sales. Having built the foundational skills for both roles and met our eligibility criteria, top graduates on this path can begin their Salesforce Solution Engineering careers. The promotion window opens from month 7 onwards. Our graduate program is a fully immersive experience, combining comprehensive learning paths with in-role experience. You will be assigned an experienced Solution Engineering Buddy who will provide hands-on coaching and involve you in some of their live deals. You will also be paired with experienced Sales Development Buddies during the Sales Rotation and you also get to call your first salesforce leads and find your first deals. Throughout the programme, you will gain exposure to senior solution engineering and sales professionals during our inspiration sessions. By joining Salesforce, you will have the opportunity to lay the foundation for a fast-paced, successful career . We are a proud member of the Fortune 100 Best Places to Work list for the past 14 years and a consistent winner of Great Place to Work awards. Who are we looking for? You are a 2025 or 2026 graduate (minimum bachelor’s degree) For the Solution Engineering Path, we consider applicants from the following academic backgrounds: Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Data Science/Data Engineering, Information Systems, or other adjacent disciplines You are a creative problem-solver You are a relationship builder and possess a growth mindset You are curious, self-motivated, and focused on continuous learning You thrive in a team environment You have excellent interpersonal skills You are goal-oriented and comfortable in a fast-paced environment You are fluent in English and Hebrew is essential What does our new EMEA Graduate Program look like? The Program Is Structured As Follows Introduction Month During your first month, you will receive extensive onboarding enablement through a Salesforce-style academy, where you will: Become immersed in the culture of Salesforce and gain a deep understanding of our values Develop an understanding of our solutions, technologies, and tools Learn critical professional skills for your career at Salesforce Follow a structured learning calendar with sessions and hands-on workshops led by experts and program alumni Rotations During the Graduate Program, you will experience both the Solution Engineering Path and the Sales Path . The structure of each rotation is similar: you will spend 60% of your time immersed in the role with clear tasks, targets, and stakeholder alignment, while the remaining 40% will focus on role-specific learning. You will be paired with experienced buddies in each path. If your first rotation (months 2 through 4) is in Solution Engineering , you will then join the Sales Graduate Rotation from months 5 through 7, and vice versa. Over these six months, you will gain exposure to both roles. The time spent mastering the fundamentals of these complementary disciplines will enable you to be more productive and impactful upon promotion. Throughout the rotations, there will be self-paced certifications and skills assessments . You must meet all eligibility criteria before you can panel for promotion . Examples Of What You Can Expect During The Rotations Solution Engineering Graduate Rotation Learn our solutions at a deeper, more technical level Work closely with the Solution Engineering organisation, supporting the creation of cutting-edge customer demonstrations Learn the art of customer discovery and how to create a compelling customer point of view Sales Graduate Rotation Learn Salesforce’s best-in-class prospecting and qualification methodologies Learn how to use social, digital, video, chat, and phone platforms to effectively engage Salesforce prospects Collaborate with Sales Development Specialists to run campaigns and help build sales pipeline for the EMEA Sales organisation What’s in it for you? A clear and structured career path within our Solution Engineering organisation The opportunity to work in an international team within a nurturing environment Access to our diverse internal employee groups A comprehensive benefits package Relocation budget and guidance throughout your relocation process An additional seven days of paid time off for charitable causes – learn more about our 1-1-1 model Map your future for the coming years With the EMEA Graduate Program - Solution Engineering Path , you can continue to progress: After completing the Graduate Program rotations, you may progress to Associate Solution Engineer, with opportunities to work across ESB, SMB, and GRB customer segments, or join our Specialist SE team. In some instances, this path may vary or be subject to change. With our strong mentoring culture, we strive to develop industry-leading Solution Engineering leaders. This is a phenomenal opportunity to build international experience within an organisation that has transformed the enterprise software market through cloud computing. Unleash Your Potential When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world. Accommodations If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form. Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options. Posting Statement Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. 6c90bf4e47596fda822e.description: Project Manager – Drug Development & Manufacturing Role Summary The Project Manager will oversee the end-to-end execution of client projects, from the initial transfer of processes through development, scale-up, and optimization, to final technology transfer or implementation within GMP manufacturing. This role is accountable for coordinating project activities, managing schedules and budgets, allocating resources, and ensuring that agreed objectives are achieved. The successful candidate will work closely with clients and internal teams to maintain alignment with project goals, regulatory obligations, and established quality standards. Acting as the central link between clients and internal stakeholders, the Project Manager will drive collaboration, facilitate decision-making, and ensure projects progress efficiently from initiation to completion. 1. Project Coordination and Execution Manage projects across the drug development and manufacturing lifecycle, ensuring activities are completed in line with agreed objectives. Define project scope, deliverables, key milestones, schedules, resource requirements, and interdependencies. Prepare and maintain comprehensive project documentation, plans, and schedules that reflect client expectations and applicable regulatory requirements. Use established project management tools and knowledge management platforms to coordinate activities and maintain project visibility. Review project performance regularly, identifying potential delays, bottlenecks, and deviations from planned outcomes. Implement corrective measures and revise priorities when necessary to maintain progress and meet commitments. Ensure seamless coordination of activities across all project workstreams. 2. Client Engagement and Communication Serve as the principal contact for clients, managing communication throughout the project lifecycle. Develop and maintain productive relationships built on trust, transparency, and consistent delivery. Agree on project expectations, responsibilities, timelines, scope, and deliverables with relevant stakeholders. Communicate progress, emerging risks, key decisions, and milestone achievements through regular updates. Respond to client questions and concerns in a timely and professional manner, coordinating solutions where required. Ensure client priorities and business objectives inform project planning and execution. Help strengthen existing partnerships and identify opportunities for continued collaboration. 3. Technical Team Coordination and Leadership Coordinate cross-functional teams involving scientific, engineering, CMC, regulatory, quality, manufacturing, and operational specialists. Establish ownership of tasks, clarify individual responsibilities, and align team priorities with project objectives. Manage interfaces between departments to support efficient workflows and timely completion of activities. Organize project meetings, monitor action items, facilitate discussions, and drive timely resolution of outstanding decisions. Provide direction and support to project contributors, encouraging accountability and ownership. Promote a collaborative working environment focused on communication, problem-solving, and shared outcomes. 4. Financial Oversight and Resource Planning Manage project financials to support delivery within approved cost parameters. Work with Finance, Operations, and technical functions to prepare project budgets and cost forecasts. Monitor actual expenditure against planned costs and identify emerging financial pressures. Communicate anticipated budget deviations and financial concerns to the appropriate stakeholders. Plan and coordinate the use of personnel, facilities, equipment, and technical capabilities. Address resource constraints proactively and escalate significant financial or capacity challenges to senior leadership and clients when appropriate. 5. Project Risks, Issues, and Change Control Evaluate potential threats to project schedules, budgets, scope, deliverables, and quality. Establish risk mitigation strategies and contingency measures to reduce the impact of identified challenges. Maintain current risk and issue registers, ensuring actions are assigned, monitored, and completed. Drive problem-solving activities and coordinate the removal of obstacles that could affect project performance. Escalate critical issues in accordance with established governance and reporting procedures. Support the implementation and follow-up of corrective and preventive actions. Assess and manage changes to project scope, schedules, costs, and deliverables through a structured change control process. 6. Quality Assurance and Regulatory Alignment Ensure project activities comply with relevant regulatory expectations, internal procedures, and applicable quality management systems. Maintain complete, accurate, and traceable project records and documentation. Verify that project outputs satisfy agreed technical requirements, quality criteria, and client expectations. Partner with Quality, Regulatory, and technical specialists to address compliance matters and resolve quality-related issues. Encourage a proactive approach to quality, documentation, procedural compliance, and continuous improvement. 7. Process Enhancement and Business Development Review existing project management practices and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, and effectiveness. Document project outcomes, capture lessons learned, and incorporate improvements into future planning. Work alongside CMC and technical specialists to design, refine, and introduce additional service capabilities. Help establish standardized processes, practical guidelines, and scalable project management approaches to support organizational growth. Collect feedback from clients and internal stakeholders to enhance service delivery and project outcomes. Contribute to the development of innovative solutions that respond to evolving client needs and increasingly complex development and manufacturing challenges. Measures of Success Performance in this position will be assessed through the ability to: Deliver projects in accordance with agreed scope, schedule, budget, and quality requirements. Establish productive client partnerships and maintain high levels of stakeholder confidence. Coordinate multidisciplinary teams effectively and achieve alignment across technical functions. Anticipate project challenges and implement timely, effective risk mitigation measures. Maintain clear, accurate, and consistent communication with internal and external stakeholders. Manage project costs, resource requirements, and financial performance responsibly. Identify and implement improvements that strengthen project execution and client satisfaction. Support the expansion of technical services, operational capabilities, and project delivery practices
