GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Technical Recruiter, you'll help GitLab build the engineering and product teams behind our DevSecOps platform. In this individual contributor role, you'll partner with leaders across Engineering, Product, Security, and UX and own searches from intake through close. You'll build inclusive pipelines and use data and market insight to guide hiring decisions, while growing into a trusted talent advisor.

What you'll do

  • Manage full-cycle searches for roles such as Backend and Frontend Engineers, Site Reliability Engineers, Security Engineers, Data Engineers, Engineering Managers, and Product Managers, delivering against agreed recruiting goals and key metrics with accurate, timely documentation in Greenhouse.
  • Lead intake and kickoff conversations to align hiring teams on role scope, technical requirements, team context, interview plans, and timelines, with senior team guidance as needed.
  • Partner with hiring teams on structured, equitable technical interviews with clear competencies and actionable feedback; challenge assumptions and escalate risks or blockers early.
  • Use talent-market research, compensation benchmarks, funnel metrics, and candidate feedback to shape search strategy and address hiring issues.
  • Assess technical candidates on depth of experience, scope and impact of past work, problem-solving, and open source or community contributions, and how well their skills fit GitLab's teams and technology.
  • Build research-based, diversity-focused sourcing plans that balance applicants, passive talent, referrals, internal talent, and targeted outreach across technical communities and specialized talent pools.
  • Deliver a thoughtful candidate experience through disciplined pipeline management, proactive communication, timely feedback, and offer negotiations that clearly explain compensation, equity, and benefits.
  • Improve recruiting practices by sharing learnings and reusable resources, using artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly, and representing GitLab's mission, values, and culture.

What you'll bring

  • Intermediate-level recruiting experience, with a track record of owning full-cycle searches independently.
  • Technical recruiting experience, or a strong interest in learning engineering and product disciplines, tech stacks, team structures, and how software is built and shipped.
  • Developing advisor skills: building stakeholder trust, influencing without authority, and managing hiring team expectations.
  • Experience building proactive, diversity-focused sourcing strategies and balanced pipelines for hard-to-fill or specialized roles.
  • A data-informed approach that turns funnel insights into practical actions.
  • Strong organization across multiple requisitions and clear written and verbal communication across time zones, with attention to detail and candidate care.
  • Experience with an applicant tracking system and recruiting tools such as Greenhouse, LinkedIn Recruiter, LinkedIn Insights, SeekOut, or comparable platforms; ability to evaluate AI-generated work, protect confidential information, and share responsible workflows with team members.
  • Experience recruiting for DevSecOps, developer tools, or open source software is helpful, not required.

About the team

We work in a globally distributed, remote-first Talent Acquisition team where clear communication and reliable follow-through matter. Our team members share learnings and create reusable resources to improve the quality and consistency of hiring across Research & Development.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

86ac399e593856126926.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Anthropic is building the Forward Deployed Engineering team to help the world's most ambitious organizations adopt Claude in ways that are transformative, safe, and lasting. Our Technical Deployment Leads (TDLs) and Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed with strategic customers to ship production AI applications that solve real business problems. Our delivery model pairs two roles: FDEs own the technical artifact, and TDLs own the engagement end to end, from statement of work (SOW) through production deployment.

As a Manager of Technical Deployment in EMEA, you lead a team of TDLs embedded with strategic customers. You own engagement portfolio health across your team, set the bar for delivery quality, and define where we play: which customers and which use cases are ready for production AI today. Your work will directly influence Anthropic's product direction and establish Anthropic as the trusted partner for AI transformation across the region. This role is based in London.

This is a player-coach role. You need to be credible in architecture conversations with a customer's engineering leads and equally comfortable in front of executive sponsors. You will also lead the most complex engagements yourself when the stakes call for it. Most of your impact will come through the people you hire and the standard you hold them to. You won't write production code, but you will pressure-test the technical decisions your TDL team makes with FDEs.

Responsibilities

  • Hire, develop, and retain a team of TDLs embedded in engagements across EMEA. Set a high bar for delivery judgment, technical fluency, and customer presence, and run the interview loop that holds that bar.
  • Manage each TDL directly: regular 1:1s, clear expectations, direct feedback, and a growth plan. Build a bench that runs engagements well without you in the room.
  • Define the delivery strategy for your portfolio: which kinds of companies we engage, which use cases we prioritize, and how that differs by market and industry. Hold each TDL accountable for a clear account strategy: what we want to achieve with the customer and the exit gates that tell us we got there.
  • Own portfolio health across your team. Track which engagements are on track, at risk, or closing out, and intervene early when delivery drifts. Run engagement quality reviews with your team.
  • Own customer outcomes across the portfolio. Hold the executive relationship with customer sponsors, run steering committees, and represent Anthropic with senior business, risk, legal, and engineering leaders.
  • Make the staffing call for each engagement. Work with FDE managers to match TDLs and engineers to each customer, and adjust as scope changes.
  • Lead the most complex engagements yourself. Take the TDL seat when engagement size, regulatory exposure, or organizational complexity calls for it, from SOW through production deployment.
  • Set the bar for delivery excellence: SOW quality, MVP scoping, and value measurement. Ensure every engagement has a defensible impact story.
  • Build regulatory requirements into how the team scopes and delivers, working with Legal, Security, and customer risk functions, so compliance shapes the plan from the start rather than blocking it late.
  • Codify reusable solution patterns, evaluation frameworks, and technical playbooks across the team. Turn what works in the field into delivery infrastructure that lets the practice scale, and adapt global playbooks to EMEA markets.
  • Partner with Sales to qualify engagements, shape scope, and inform SOWs. Partner with Marketing and Sales on EMEA go-to-market materials, reference cases, and positioning.
  • Run the team's operating rhythm: engagement reviews, knowledge-sharing, and escalation support, and feed the wider post-sales cadence and dashboards. Set team goals tied to customer outcomes.
  • Bring the field back to Anthropic. Surface delivery lessons and emerging use cases from EMEA to Product and Research, and represent the region in leadership discussions.
  • Consistently uphold Anthropic's values as you lead your team. TDLs should be strong representatives of Anthropic's culture as they work within customer environments.
  • Travel to customer sites across EMEA (25–50% expected), with occasional travel to the US.

You May Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 8+ years leading enterprise AI/ML delivery, whether you came up as a founder, engineer, data scientist, or researcher and moved into deployments, with at least 3 years directly managing people who owned delivery outcomes.
  • Have a track record of building and leading technical delivery teams in enterprise environments across more than one EMEA market, ideally including embedded or forward-deployed teams working at client sites.
  • Have delivered AI/ML or LLM-based agentic solutions into production. You understand solution patterns, integration approaches, and what breaks in real environments.
  • Bring depth in at least one industry (e.g., financial services, healthcare and life sciences). You understand how security, compliance, and regulatory review shape what ships, and you can speak credibly with a CIO, a chief risk officer, and a head of engineering.
  • Know the EMEA enterprise landscape: how buying and procurement differ across markets, and how regulatory requirements affect what customers can deploy.
  • Can navigate architecture discussions with engineering stakeholders, evaluate technical trade-offs, and judge whether a proposed agent design is realistic.
  • Have experience with value-based scoping, including TCO/ROI quantification and post-deployment impact measurement.
  • Thrive in ambiguity and bring structure where none exists. You have built a team, practice, or function from an early stage.
  • Have executive presence: polished, credible, and concise with senior leaders in high-stakes settings, and just as effective in a hands-on engagement review with your team.
  • Have strong written and verbal communication skills. You can translate technical complexity into clear narratives for diverse audiences. Working proficiency in a second European language such as German or French is a plus.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
£190,000—£230,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Dolby doesn't just create technologies. We shape how the world's most compelling stories are experienced in the cinema, at home, on the road, and everywhere in between. The Digital Experiences Manager is responsible for making that same impact felt across EMEA's digital channels. You'll get inside the minds of regional audiences and craft digital experiences that feel tailored to them. That means spotting the stories worth telling, finding the angle that makes them land, and working with cross functional teams to bring them to life. You'll do it as part of a global team with shared standards, shared frameworks, and a shared ambition. The job is knowing how to work within that framework, and when to push beyond it for your market. You'll be embedded in Dublin, one of Europe's most creatively connected cities, working across markets from the UK and Ireland, to France, Germany, Spain, and Netherlands. You'll need both the cultural radar to read those markets and the operational discipline to create consistency across them. Identify regional audience needs, cultural nuances, and market opportunities that should inform how global digital strategies are adapted and activated locally. Generate editorial ideas and creative angles in response to cultural moments, product launches, and audience interests across the region. Partner with Social, Creative, and other cross-functional teams to define requirements and brief in ideas that go beyond standard campaign execution. Ensure EMEA digital channels feel alive, timely, and relevant to audiences who are passionate about entertainment. Campaign Activation & Cross-Channel Coordination Lead regional campaign activation across owned digital channels, ensuring integrated, high-quality execution that reflects global campaign intent. Coordinate with Creative, CRM, Social, and regional marketing teams to ensure assets, messaging, and timelines are aligned across channels. Bring a connected-channel mindset to campaign delivery, helping ensure EMEA digital experiences complement and extend broader cross-channel activation. Performance, Insights & Optimization Own regional digital performance monitoring and optimization, tracking key metrics across owned channels including traffic, engagement, and conversion. Maintain regional dashboards and deliver proactive performance reporting to EMEA and global stakeholders. Lead A/B testing and content optimization initiatives for the region, translating insights into actionable improvements. Surface regional trends, audience signals, and optimization opportunities to inform both local and global strategy. SEO & Content Discoverability Apply global SEO and GEO frameworks to EMEA content, ensuring regional experiences are discoverable across search and AI-driven discovery environments. Lead on-page optimization, metadata management, and keyword-driven content improvements for the region. Monitor EMEA organic performance and proactively identify local search optimization opportunities. Governance, Enablement & Stakeholder Partnership Champion global content standards and governance frameworks within EMEA, ensuring consistent adoption across regional teams and programs. Serve as the primary digital point of contact for EMEA regional marketing stakeholders, building trusted partnerships that support effective digital collaboration. Provide feedback on platform usability, workflow gaps, and regional needs to inform global digital operations and roadmap planning. Qualifications What you bring A genuine point of view on what good digital experience looks like, and the portfolio to back it up. We're not looking for someone who executes briefs. We're looking for someone who can improve them. An editorial instinct. You notice the stories other people miss, and you know how to frame them for a digital audience. 5 to 7 years in digital marketing, content strategy, or digital experience management, ideally with exposure to both regional and global marketing contexts. Regional performance data is reliable, actionable, and shared proactively with stakeholders. EMEA regional marketing partners view this role as a trusted strategic and execution collaborator. Global digital standards are consistently applied and championed across the region. 87944b268ab19c9d096f.description:
Fin, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.

Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.

Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.

Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What's the opportunity? 

We’re looking for a proven operator to redesign how Customer Support works across Human and AI Support. Fin is an AI-first support organisation, and our processes should reflect that: you’ll have a genuine licence to rethink, rebuild or retire existing processes from first principles, not just refine them. This is a hands-on and strategic role: you keep day-to-day operations running well and fix what is broken, while building a long-term process strategy for the whole of Customer Support. You will also help embed Continuous Improvement, using conversation and quality insights to decide what we fix, retrain and prioritise next.

Support at Fin changes constantly, and our processes need to keep pace with this level of change. The right candidate is exceptionally customer-focused, comes from a customer-facing background, and has experience leading and managing processes and workflows in a large organisation. You bring clear opinions and recommendations, work with a high degree of autonomy, and hold the line on the customer experience when working with other teams. You combine exceptional project management and attention to detail with a data-driven mindset and a proven ability to influence and collaborate at every level of the organisation.

What will I be doing? 

Strategy and ownership

  • Challenge and, where warranted, completely redesign existing processes and ways of working: you won’t be constrained by ‘how we’ve always done it’, and you’ll have the support of Customer Support leadership to make bold changes
  • Own and evolve the framework for reviewing, prioritising and implementing Customer Support processes and workflows across Human and AI Support, so every change improves the customer experience
  • Build and maintain a long-term process strategy and roadmap for Support, balancing quick wins and immediate fixes with strategic improvements 
  • Own the long-term Continuous Improvement strategy for Support, setting priorities and a roadmap that cover both Human and AI support
  • Bring clear proposals and recommendations to leadership, and act on them with autonomy
  • Partner with teams outside of Customer Support to design processes that work end to end, agreeing clear ownership, handoffs and shared goals so the customer experience holds across team boundaries.

Process design and improvement

  • Analyse current processes across Human and AI Support and decide whether each should be improved, redesigned from scratch or removed entirely. Where AI and automation can fundamentally change how the work gets done, lead that transformation rather than layering them onto legacy workflows
  • Own day-to-day operational process fixes and keep existing processes effective
  • Design and roll out new or improved processes, solo or with SMEs, partnering closely with Customer Support leaders and ICs in every region so processes work globally, not just for one region
  • Design and implement process control metrics, and monitor process performance and KPIs
  • Use data to find where processes are failing, size the opportunity and prove the impact of changes, building and maintaining dashboards and reports that give leaders a clear view of process health across Human and AI support
  • Ensure compliance with internal policies and external regulations

Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain and iterate on the Continuous Improvement framework, using insights from both Human and AI support to drive improvements, across Enablement, Quality, AI support, etc.
  • Turn insights into a prioritised improvement backlog, with clear owners across respective internal teams
  • Track whether each improvement worked, using before-and-after measures such as repeat contact rate, resolution rate and CX
  • Turn customer conversation data into clear, actionable insights for Product, Engineering and other teams, giving them evidence to shape priorities and roadmap decisions

Stakeholders and delivery

  • Hold the line on the customer experience with cross-functional partners, challenging constructively when a proposed change would compromise the customer
  • Partner and collaborate with cross-functional teams to build and maintain processes and related training
  • Take full ownership of large, cross-functional special projects that improve the customer experience, increase teammate efficiency and engagement, and drive company goals
  • Communicate and engage on all process and continuous improvement changes with Customer Support and the wider organisation

What skills do I need? 

  • Experience: 4+ years in Customer Support or a customer-facing role, including 2+ years in process management or continuous improvement and 2+ years in project or program management
  • Strong technical capability: You are hands-on and credible in a complex SaaS tech stack, including CRM systems such as Salesforce. You can configure workflows, integrations and automations yourself rather than relying on others to build them. Experience with system integrations or process harmonisation is a bonus.
  • AI and automation: Proven track record of using AI and automation to drive improvements, ideally in an AI-first or SaaS support organisation. Knowledge of Fin (previously Intercom) is a strong advantage.
  • Improvement frameworks: Strong knowledge of process and continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Kaizen, etc.)
  • Data and strategy: You analyse data, turn it into clear insights for stakeholders, and build a long-term process strategy and roadmap that becomes practical, prioritised plans
  • Ownership: A self-starter who delivers complex programs with minimal guidance, forms a point of view and brings proposals rather than questions
  • Influence: Confident and credible with senior leaders and cross-functional partners. You challenge constructively and hold the line on the customer experience.
  • Collaboration: Strong communicator who builds rapport quickly with technical and non-technical colleagues and involves frontline teammates early

#LI-Hybrid

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Offerings vary by location in line with local practices and requirements. Learn more about working at Fin and the benefits we offer at fin.ai/careers. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Salesforce will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. 

Policies 

Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.

We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. As an organization, our policy is to not advocate on behalf of the company or our employees on any social or political topics out of our internal or external communications. We respect personal opinion and expression on these topics on personal social platforms on personal time, and do not challenge or confront anyone for their views on non-work related topics. Our goal is to focus on doing incredible work to achieve our goals and unite the company through our core values.  

Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.

88172273b9c07c08f486.description: Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented. The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code. We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n. We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe. The Role You own Banking Experience: the accounts at the center of customer's relationship with the bank, and the API and dashboards they use to manage them. In this role you’re responsible for redefining what beautiful software in banking looks like. You'll define account structures that give customers powerful building blocks for their products, and craft intuitive interfaces grounded in a deep understanding of their use cases and workflows. You report to Will, Head of Product, and work closely with Simon, our CTO. You're expected to operate with full autonomy on your team's roadmap, collaborating with design and engineering. Your First Six Months Months 1-2: Take over day-to-day ownership of the Banking Experience team - the roadmap, the ways of working, the hard decisions. Establish yourself with customers and how they use our accounts. You define and ship your first project. Months 3-4: Execution mode. You're unblocking engineering daily, making hard prioritization calls, and shipping your roadmap to customers. 886acab9bcc56d40255b.description: About us   Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort,   Photoroom   is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.  We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.  We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.     Role Summary   We're looking for an  SMB Go-To-Market Lead  to own how Photoroom wins established eCommerce merchants doing €500K to tens of millions in GMV (gross merchandise value, i.e., annual online sales).  You come from the eCommerce world. You know where these merchants spend their time, which platforms they run on (Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, TikTok Shop, and the agencies and apps around them), and which channels actually move them. You've already acquired merchants at this scale, and you've done it with campaigns people talked about.  This is a  lead  role. You'll ship campaigns yourself every month, and you'll lead a team of 2 GTM managers focused on dedicated personas.  This is a marketing lead role for someone who still loves making the work, not a manager who has stopped shipping.    Compensation:  €80,000 – €110,000 + BSPCE   Location:  Paris, in-office 3 days per week     About the Role      Own SMB merchant acquisition and revenue  - Set the GTM strategy for established eCommerce brands and own the numbers behind it: new merchant acquisition and conversion to paid users. Report on them monthly, and decide where the next euro goes across your channels.     Build the B2B channels we don't have yet  - Set up and scale outbound, partnerships (eCom platforms, app ecosystems, agencies, marketplaces), in-person events, and LinkedIn. Find which ones work for merchants at €500K+ GMV, prove them, then turn them into repeatable playbooks.     Create campaigns people talk about  - Concept, write, and ship launch and brand campaigns that spread across eCommerce communities and social feeds. You have the creative idea and know how to distribute it.     Stay hands-on  - Personally run at least one major campaign or channel bet each quarter, end to end. Set the bar for the team by doing the work, not just reviewing it.     Lead and grow a team of   2 , two GTM managers, each owning a merchant persona. Set clear goals, coach weekly, hire well as the team grows.     Be the voice of the merchant  - Turn what you hear from merchants, partners, and the market into positioning, messaging, and input for Product.     Orchestrate campaigns across Marketing  - Work hand in hand with our Paid User Acquisition, PR, and SEO/GEO teams. Bring them into every campaign from the brief, so paid, earned, and organic efforts land together and amplify each other.     Measure everything  - Track impact from first touch to paying merchant, report on CAC (customer acquisition cost) and payback by channel, and kill what doesn't work fast.       About you   You know eCommerce merchants from the inside, and you have the results and the campaigns to show for it.     8+ years in GTM, product marketing (PMM), or marketing in the eCommerce industry  - At an eCom platform, a SaaS for merchants, a marketplace, an agency, or a fast-growing DTC brand.     A track record of acquiring merchants at scale  - You've acquired eCommerce merchants at scale, including established brands doing €500K to tens of millions in GMV. You can walk us through the numbers. You know the platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Etsy…), their app stores and partner programs, the agencies and the communities where merchants make decisions.     Proven in B2B channels  - You've personally run outbound, partnerships, in-person events, or LinkedIn programs that generated pipeline.     Strong creative background  - You've led campaigns that went viral or became the reference in their category. You have taste, you can write, and you can brief and judge creative work.     A player-coach who still ships  - You're excited to lead a small team and make them better, while still doing the work yourself. Prior management experience is a plus, not a requirement.     Data-driven  - You set up tracking and attribution, read the numbers yourself, and make calls on them.     Fluent in modern AI tools  - Like every great marketer today, you use AI in your daily work to go faster.     Autonomous with proactive transparency  - You share plans early, keep the team informed, and communicate openly so everyone stays aligned.     Fluent English  (we exclusively work in English)    If you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still apply. We'd love to chat and see if you could be a great fit.    Bonus points    You've worked at or with Shopify, an eCom platform, or a top app in its ecosystem.    You have an existing network of eCom founders, agencies, and partners in Europe or the US.    You've built or grown a community of merchants or creators.    You've worked in a fast-growing AI or product-led growth (PLG) company, where users sign up and buy without talking to sales.      What you’ll ship in your first 90 days     A channel plan for established merchants . Which of outbound, partnerships, events, and LinkedIn we test first, the target for each, and the budget.     A first outbound engine . A targeted list of €500K+ GMV brands, persona-tailored sequences, and at least 5K merchants reached through it.     A partnership with a platform, app, or agency . Co-marketing that puts Photoroom in front of thousands of merchants.      Benefits     Regular team gatherings,  including in-person onboarding in Paris (1–2 weeks), yearly company offsite, team retreats, and quarterly in-person meetings     25 days annual leave  + RTT and local public holidays     Competitive equity package  with BSPCE     €1,000 annual learning and development budget      Private health insurance      Access to personalized mental health support  via MokaCare     Sports and cultural activities reimbursement      Relocation support (up to €10k)  for those choosing to move to France (visa + housing support)     Note: Visa sponsorship and relocation support are only available for roles based in France.     Hiring Process    Screening call with Talent Manager (30 min)    Technical interview with Hiring Manager (45 min)    Take-home assignment and live review with the team (45 min)    Culture fit interviews and meet the team (~3h total)    Reference check and offer     Support:  We value diversity and aim to create an inclusive experience for all applicants. Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to make the process more accessible for you.    Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging  We're committed to enabling everyone to feel included and valued at work. We believe our company and culture are strongest when composed of diverse experiences and backgrounds.  That's also why we have flexible working hours, trust people to work in a hybrid environment, and extended parental leave.  All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, family, gender identity, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are hiring Support Engineers to serve as the named, dedicated Product Support point of contact for Anthropic's most strategic enterprise customers. As a Support Engineer, you'll be providing high-touch, deeply contextual support to a defined book of accounts — embedded in your customers' shared channels, known by name to their stakeholders, and partnering closely with Sales, Customer Success, and Applied AI as the technical support voice on the account team. You'll bring deep knowledge of how each of your customers is built on Claude to every interaction, so you can investigate, diagnose, and resolve their most complex technical needs with nuance and speed — and ensure the right internal teams are engaged when needed. Responsibilities Serve as the named technical support contact for a defined book of strategic enterprise accounts, embedded in customer channels and joining recurring account cadences as the support voice Own your customers' technical support needs end to end — investigate, diagnose, and resolve complex issues directly, and partner with internal Engineering and Product teams to drive resolution when needed Build deep, durable context on each customer's architecture, integrations, and use cases so you can respond with nuance rather than from a script Partner closely with the Customer Success Manager, Account Executive, and Applied AI team on each account as part of a single, coordinated account team Capture technical feedback and product friction from your accounts and route it to Product with the impact data and detail needed to prioritize it correctly Manage high-urgency issues for your accounts with extreme ownership, and coordinate cleanly with the broader Product Support team for continuous coverage Help build the foundations of the Support Engineer function — runbooks, escalation paths, tooling, and the metrics we'll use to measure its value Become an expert in all Anthropic products across the API, Claude for Enterprise, and Claude Code You may be a good fit if you Have 5+ years in technical product support, with meaningful time in an escalated, priority, or named-account support team for enterprise customers Have been the person an enterprise customer knows by name and reaches for first when they need technical help Are deeply fluent with APIs and technical SaaS products, and can read technical documentation, error logs, and request traces with ease Have hands-on experience troubleshooting SSO, SAML, OAuth, and enterprise authentication flows Are persistent and curious — you delight in the hunt of tracking down a bug, and are energized by fixing it for every similar user going forward Possess strong user empathy and crisp, kind written communication; you can translate between a frustrated customer engineer and an internal platform team without losing either Are comfortable operating in ambiguity, making informed decisions in never-before-seen situations, and knowing when to pull the escalation cord Enjoy building trust and collaborating closely with go-to-market partners (Sales, CS, Applied AI) without owning the commercial relationship yourself Have contributed to the foundations of a support team before — the essential, often unglamorous work of writing the first runbook Are excited about Anthropic's products and the opportunity to shape how the world's largest companies get support for them Strong candidates may also have SQL proficiency for querying logs and usage data to investigate issues Comfort with command line interfaces and basic scripting (Bash, Python, JavaScript) Understanding of LLM capabilities, prompt engineering patterns, and current limitations Familiarity with enterprise networking concepts, cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP), and IT environments Experience working inside a customer's shared Slack or similar embedded-support model Background as a Technical Account Manager, Support Engineer, or Designated/Premier Support contact at a developer-platform or infrastructure company The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $210,000 - $250,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. 88c5f17500e4954c139b.description: Job Description Why Start Your Career at S&W? Starting your career is about more than just a job. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that shape you. Whether that's passing an exam, achieving a personal milestone or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that's invested in your growth, celebrates your successes and supports you to be yourself. At S&W, you'll be given meaningful work from day one, while having the support, training and encouragement to help you succeed. You'll learn by doing, working alongside experienced colleagues, contributing to real projects and developing valuable professional skills from the start. As your confidence grows, so will your opportunities, with plenty of support along the way. As a growing accountancy and advisory firm, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. You'll learn from people at every level of the business, gain exposure to a variety of clients, industries and experiences, and develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to build a successful career. The Audit & Assurance Team at S&W Our Audit & Assurance team works with a diverse range of clients, from entrepreneurial and family-owned businesses to charities, not-for-profit organisations and larger established businesses across a variety of industries. What sets Audit & Assurance at S&W apart is the breadth of experience you'll gain early in your career. You'll develop technical expertise, commercial awareness and a well-rounded understanding of how organisations operate, while working closely with experienced colleagues and gaining exposure to senior leaders and Partners. Together, this provides a strong foundation for a successful career in the profession. What Will You Be Doing? As part of our Audit & Assurance team, you'll work alongside colleagues to deliver services to a variety of clients. You'll be involved in different stages of an engagement, gaining insight into how organisations operate and the role assurance plays in building confidence in financial reporting. Alongside your role, you'll study towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification. Through a combination of professional training and practical experience, you'll build a strong foundation in audit, accountancy and wider business advisory services. You'll be supported with funded training, dedicated study time and guidance from colleagues who have successfully completed the qualification themselves. Your work will include: Analysing financial information Testing processes and controls Building relationships with client teams Resolving audit and accountancy queries Supporting a range of audit and accountancy projects Whether you're based in one of our offices or working directly with clients, you'll contribute to meaningful work from day one while building the skills and confidence needed to become a trusted adviser. To Be Successful in This Role You'll be someone who: Is curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges Enjoys working with others and building positive relationships Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems Is proactive and looks for ways to make a positive contribution Takes ownership of their development and is motivated to achieve their goals You'll also need to: Be committed to working towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification Have some accountancy experience, as part of your education or work experience Have obtained or be predicted a minimum 2:2 degree, in any discipline Minimum 400 Leaving Certificate points (or equivalent) Leaving Certificate O2 or H5 in Maths and English (or equivalent) Your Learning & Development We'll support you throughout your qualification journey with a leading UK training provider, dedicated study time and practical experience that complements your learning. You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from a support network that includes experienced colleagues, a buddy and our Learning & Development team, helping you make the most of the opportunities available to you. As a Colleague at S&W, You'll Have Access to Benefits That Include Fully funded training towards professional qualifications Competitive salary Private medical insurance Life assurance Pension contribution Generous holiday package Option to purchase additional holiday Cycle to work scheme Season ticket loan Eye care support Shared parental leave Our Commitment to Inclusion We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. We are happy to make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate for your needs throughout the application process. Please let your Recruiter know. If you're unsuccessful, you'll need to wait until the following recruitment season to reapply. 88d835e1d1702b0bed55.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We believe powerful AI can compress a century of scientific progress into a decade. Claude Science is a big part of building toward that future.

Claude Science is an AI workbench that gives researchers a single environment for work that today spans dozens of disconnected tools — literature, specialized databases, scientific computing, analysis, and publication-ready outputs. Claude Science already renders protein structures, genome tracks, and chemical structures natively, and coordinates multi-agent workflows with built-in review for citation and calculation errors — and we're just getting started. Much of this is being built 0→1 right now, in a category no one has defined yet.

We're growing the Claude Science product team. As a Product Manager on Claude Science, you will own a major area of the roadmap end to end — think expanding into new scientific fields, landing new model capabilities with researchers, or making the workbench ready for enterprise R&D teams — and help shape the overall product direction alongside the rest of the team. You'll spend real time with researchers in academic labs, biotech and pharma R&D, and research institutes to understand how science actually gets done — from hypothesis to analysis to publication and beyond— and turn what you learn into shipped product. You'll partner directly with our research teams to make the models better at science, help decide which fields and workflows we go after next, and shape what it takes for Claude Science to be trusted in enterprise and regulated research environments.

We're looking for experienced product managers and founders with real scientific or technical depth: people who can hold their own in a conversation with a structural biologist or a computational chemist, get in the weeds of model transcripts and evals, and still zoom out to help define a product category. You thrive in ambiguity, uncover non-obvious use cases for nascent capabilities, and bring those insights back to research.

Our north star is for Claude Science to accelerate scientific progress — across biology, chemistry, physics, and beyond — from early discovery through real-world application, by an order of magnitude.

Key responsibilities

  • Own vision, strategy, roadmap, and execution for a major area of Claude Science, and contribute to overall product direction in a category that is still being defined
  • Spend meaningful time with working scientists — in interviews, working sessions, and key customer conversations — and synthesize what you learn into clear priorities, requirements, and success metrics
  • Partner with research to make Claude better at science: define target behaviors, build and shape evals grounded in real scientific workflows, surface failure modes from real usage, and feed them back into model development
  • Drive model and feature launches in your area end to end: define readiness criteria, coordinate across research, engineering, design, and go-to-market, run early access programs, and make sure launches land well with researchers
  • Identify which scientific domains, data sources, tools, and integrations Claude Science should support next, and build the case with evidence from users, usage data, and the broader landscape
  • Prototype ideas yourself with Claude to validate them before committing engineering time
  • Work with safeguards, policy, security, and go-to-market partners so that powerful scientific capabilities reach trusted researchers responsibly, including in enterprise and regulated research settings
  • Drive enterprise readiness  — security and compliance reviews, admin and deployment controls, and the procurement realities of pharma and biotech — so large organizations can adopt it with confidence
  • Prioritize ruthlessly across a broad surface — scientific domains, customer segments, and competing workflows — and make clear calls on what our products serve deeply first, holding the line on MVP versus ideal state
  • Define how success is measured for AI research and development products — adoption and retention among working scientists and operators, time-to-result on real analyses, trust in outputs — and use those measures to steer planning
  • Maintain an objective, current view of the AI-for-science ecosystem — models, tools, benchmarks, and competitors — and of where Claude Science stands within it

Minimum qualifications

  • Have product management experience shipping technical products in close partnership with engineering and design, or equivalent experience driving product direction as a founder, engineer, or scientist
  • Have a scientific or deeply technical background — enough to reason with domain experts about their workflows and to diagnose where and why a model is falling short on a scientific task
  • Have a strong grasp of AI and LLM concepts, use AI tools daily, and are comfortable going deep on model behavior, prompting, and evaluation methodology
  • Are data-driven: you ground prioritization in usage data, eval results, and evidence from users rather than intuition alone
  • Have strong user empathy and can synthesize vague or contradictory feedback from expert users into actionable priorities
  • Navigate and execute amid ambiguity as a first-principles thinker, flexing across scientific domains based on the problem at hand and finding simple, easy-to-understand solutions
  • Communicate clearly in writing and can align research, engineering, and go-to-market stakeholders through influence rather than authority
  • Think carefully and creatively about the risks and benefits of putting frontier scientific capabilities into the world, beyond past checklists and playbooks

Preferred qualifications

  • 8+ years in product management or equivalent product leadership, including taking products from 0 to 1 and scaling them; founder experience is a plus
  • An advanced degree or hands-on research experience in biology, chemistry, physics, materials science, or a related field — or experience building software for scientists (e.g., computational biology, cheminformatics, lab informatics, simulation, or scientific data platforms)
  • Have personally built evals or benchmarks for model capabilities, ideally agentic or scientific ones
  • Experience shipping products into life sciences, pharma, or other regulated research environments, including familiarity with their data governance and compliance expectations
  • A track record of launching ambitious products that found distribution or commercial success
  • Experience designing trusted-access or staged-rollout programs for sensitive capabilities
  • A creative, hacker spirit and a love of solving hard puzzles

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$305,000—$385,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Want to see the systems you engineer come to life on site? Launch your career with us and open a world of opportunities! Overview NeoDyne is a leading engineering company specialising in industrial automation, digital manufacturing, and electrical engineering solutions. With a strong presence across multiple sectors, including Life Sciences, Food & Beverage, and Energy, NeoDyne delivers leading-edge solutions that drive efficiency, safety, and performance for its customers worldwide. We develop high-availability automation and electrical systems for mission-critical industries, including pharmaceutical manufacturing, data centres, and energy infrastructure, ensuring continuous operation and compliance. We additionally integrate emerging technologies to enhance control, scalability, and operational insight. Our expertise also extends to power generation, natural gas transmission, and high-voltage system design, delivering robust solutions that strengthen critical infrastructure. With a team of 230+ skilled engineers, our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle, from design and implementation to commissioning and operations. From our offices in Ireland, the UK, Romania, and the US, we operate on a global scale, combining technical expertise with local delivery. We support customers across Europe, North America, and Asia, delivering tailored engineering services that drive long-term success. Position Summary NeoDyne are recruiting a Graduate Automation Engineer to join our expanding System Integration team. Our graduate programme is all about learning new and developing your existing skills. Over a two-year period, you will be placed in projects where you get to do meaningful work and contribute to the business. This Graduate opportunity is offered as a full-time permanent contract, based at our Dublin Office , with an excellent salary and benefits package. If successful, you will enjoy NeoDyne's "People First" company culture, built on mutual respect, trust, and honesty, where each individual actively contributes as a valued team member. What might I be doing? Over a two-year period, you will be placed in projects where you get to do meaningful work and contribute to the business. Projects will be spread across all areas of Industrial Automation and could include PLC and SCADA design, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), control logic programming, control panel hardware design, and site testing & commissioning. Generating technical documentation and dealing with customers will also be key parts of our graduate programme to help develop your soft skills. You will also have the opportunity to travel to customer sites to get involved in installation, testing, and commissioning. What about training? Our induction programme revolves around a 70-20-10 model for learning and development. 70% On-the-job Learning: You'll get stuck in from Day 1, working on real projects, delivering real business value to our customers both on- and off-site. 20% Learning from others: You'll be part of a team, working with subject matter experts and interacting with our customers daily. You'll receive support and guidance, and an invaluable opportunity to learn from former graduates who've seen it and done it. 10% Formal Education: We'll help you become an expert in your chosen field, backed up by formal e-learning and classroom training. This extends to attaining professional certifications where relevant to our business specialisations. Required Experience & skills Level 8 Degree in Electrical/ Automation/ Mechanical/ Instrument Engineering, or equivalent. Full Irish driving license or to be achieved within 12 months of starting the role. Desired 0-2 years' experience in a similar manufacturing process improvement role or Work Placement. Experience programming PLCs Characteristics We look for candidates who Work well as part of a team. Have excellent problem solving and diagnostic skills. Can complete tasks independently, capable of self-learning. Can prioritise and coordinate work. Have excellent customer service, interpersonal, communication and organisational skills. Can multitask and work well under pressure. Are a strategic business thinker. What's on offer? Competitive starting salary with year-on-year bonuses and salary increases Paid Overtime Paid Graduation Day Health Insurance Income Protection Life Assurance PRSA pension with employer contribution Flexible Working Personalised Career Development Plan Professional Certifications, pathways to become a Chartered Engineer Cycle to work scheme Apply today! With our diverse range of business specialisations, customers, and industries that we serve, we offer an unrivalled programme designed to accelerate your personal and professional development. Don't miss this opportunity to join a company at the forefront of industrial automation projects in Ireland, the UK, mainland Europe and the US. So why wait? Apply Today! NeoDyne Ltd. is an equal opportunity employer, and all applications will be treated in strictest confidence.

Working within an Agile product delivery model, this role contributes to both the continuous evolution of integration capabilities and the stability of core data flows. The Integration Engineer partners closely with Platform Engineers, Product Managers, and Data teams to deliver cohesive, end-to-end technology solutions. 89980f59236fa0c67ed6.description: Location/office policy: Molesworth Street- 3 days per week in office Start date: September 2027 Salary: €34,500 This role is being offered as a 3.5 year training contract Ready to start your career at AIB? If you're curious, ambitious and looking for a role where you can learn, grow and make a real impact from day one, our Finance Data Analyst Graduate Programme could be the perfect fit. At AIB, we know that starting your career is a big step. That's why we've created a graduate programme that gives you meaningful work, plenty of support and opportunities to develop both professionally and personally. Over 3.5 years, you'll rotate across different teams, gain exposure to exciting projects and develop the skills, experience and confidence needed to build a successful career. No two days will be the same! Why join our graduate programme? As part of the programme, you'll get the opportunity to experience different areas across Finance Data, working with a range of teams and colleagues. You'll learn on the job, contribute to real business initiatives and work alongside experienced professionals who are invested in helping you succeed. Along The Way, You'll Also Have Opportunities To Build your professional network Attend development events Connect with senior leaders across the organisation Learn from graduates who have already completed the programme Explore different career paths within AIB This is more than just a graduate role. It's an opportunity to discover what you're capable of. What You’ll Do We’re made up of small teams where you have the chance to expand your knowledge and be heavily involved in new and ongoing projects. We view inclusion & diversity, wellbeing and continuous learning & development as key enablers that help our business to grow and deliver AIB’s strategic and financial objectives. As part of the programme, you will gain exposure to some of the following: Learn the AIB Project Methodology through involvement in numerous projects including how to draft a technical specification Data visualisation skills development from maintenance of existing dashboards to building dashboards from scratch, learning scripting language, and implementing complex data visualisation solutions. Complete a journey of SQL competence from basic queries to complex scripts. Exposure to working with Teradata (Relational Database Management System), other AIB systems and platforms and a knowledge of the development of Financial Data. Data analysis and cleansing. Gathering Data Development requirements and documenting technical specifications. Running Financial Information Management reports. Monitoring data visualisation batches and fixing issues. Troubleshooting issues and implementing fixes. There will be at least 1 rotation, where we will challenge you to ensure your learning and development potential is maximised over the duration of the programme. Skills Graduates on this programme are given the opportunity to attend online courses in UCD to supplement on the job learning . There you will be able to develop a range of important skills, including practical data manipulation, visualisation, analytics, and machine learning. The programme assessment is project based enabling you to demonstrate your understanding and familiarity of each semester’s content in a work themed, practical way. On completion of the programme, you will receive the following from UCD: Diploma in Data Analysis without Coding Diploma in Database Fundamentals Certificate in Python Programming Diploma in Data Analytics: Visualisation Diploma in Data Analytics: Machine Learning Specialist Certificate in Data Analytics What's in it for you? Alongside Valuable Experience And Development Opportunities, You'll Enjoy 21 Days annual leave & 2 additional volunteer days Additional AIB Bank Holidays – Good Friday & the day after St. Stephens Day Hybrid working, 3 days in office & 2 working from home Rotations across different teams Strong emphasis on wellbeing & work-life balance Structured learning & development programme Defined Contribution Pension Scheme Vhi Healthcare scheme Variable remuneration scheme We are with you every step of the way Starting your first professional role can feel daunting, but we'll be with you every step of the way. Every graduate is assigned a dedicated People Leader who will support your development, help you navigate challenges and encourage you to get the most from your experience. You'll also become part of a vibrant graduate community, joining fellow Finance Data graduates as well as graduates from previous intakes. Whether it's learning, networking or social events, you'll quickly build relationships that last well beyond the programme. We also offer access to a wide range of support networks and initiatives, including our Employee Assistance Programme and Mentor Her programme. Entry Requirements Achieved or expected to achieve a minimum 2.1 Honours Degree (or equivalent for universities outside of Ireland) is a prerequisite for those joining the AIB graduate programme. Candidates must be fully authorised to work in Ireland or hold a valid work permit for the full duration of the contract (September 2027 – March 2031). If you are not sure about your suitability based on any aspects of the role advertised, we encourage you to please contact our Future Talent Programmes team at Grads@aib.ie for a conversation. AIB is an equal opportunities employer, and we pride ourselves on being the first bank in Ireland to receive the Investors in Diversity Gold Standard accreditation from the Irish Centre for Diversity. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees. Should you have a reasonable accommodation request please email the Talent Acquisition team at Grads@aib.ie Apply today and start shaping your future with AIB. Applications are expected to close on the 26th October 2026 however, we encourage candidates to apply early as the programme may close sooner if demand is high. Eligibility and Equal Opportunities Applicants must be resident in the Republic of Ireland and be fully authorised to work, or hold a valid work permit, for the full duration of the programme. Any offer of employment will be conditional upon satisfactory evidence of the right to work in the Republic of Ireland. AIB is an equal opportunities employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates and are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. Disclaimer Unsolicited CV’s sent to AIB by Recruitment Agencies will not be accepted for this position. AIB operates a direct sourcing model and where agency assistance is required, the Talent Acquisition team will engage directly with our recruitment partners.

As we scale towards 800 aircraft and 300m passengers annually, our digital products must grow even faster — delivering simple, seamless, and high‑performance experiences for our customers. We’re looking for a driven, commercially focused App Project Manager who can take ownership of their product area, keep delivery moving at pace, and present regular updates on digital initiatives to C‑suite stakeholders. You will understand the customer, know the KPIs inside out, and work cross‑functionally to turn ideas into live improvements that enhance the travel experience and drive revenue. This is a high‑impact role where clarity, pace, and accountability are key — and where your work reaches millions of customers. What You’ll Be Doing Present regular updates on digital initiatives to C‑suite stakeholders , ensuring they have clear visibility of progress, priorities, and risks. Build a deep understanding of the customer , using insights, data, and research to identify pain points and opportunities across the digital journey. Gather and translate business needs into clear requirements , shaping simple, customer‑focused solutions with designers and project owners. Partner with development teams to define delivery plans, manage priorities, and drive projects forward in a fast‑paced environment. Manage changes, risks, and dependencies , ensuring alignment with digital and commercial objectives. Evaluate performance post‑launch , reporting key results and identifying future improvements or quick wins. Communicate clearly and proactively , ensuring the right stakeholders receive the right information at the right time. What You Need 2-3+ years’ experience in digital project management, digital transformation, or product delivery. Experience presenting updates or reports to senior and executive‑level stakeholders , including C‑suite. Experience partnering with UX/UI designers and digital delivery teams. Strong skills in process design, analysis, and documentation . A data‑driven mindset with the ability to identify opportunities quickly. Experience working in agile, fast‑moving, customer‑focused digital environments . Experience with web or app e‑commerce platforms is an advantage. Strong communication skills with excellent attention to detail. Competitive salary Discounted and unlimited travel to over 250 destinations Defined Contribution Pension Scheme Death in Service Benefit – Up to 2 times of annual basic salary 20 Days Annual Leave – Increasing to 22 days after 12 months and 25 days after 3 years of continuous service.
